Among what indicates this is also that the verses would not be proportionate in length unless we divide the last verse into two, because if you say: ﴿Guide us to the straight path [6] The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray﴾, that verse becomes long in comparison with the rest of the verses, and so it is not proportionate to them.

In any case, the preponderant and definite view is that the beginning of al-Fatihah is ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, and that the basmalah is not part of it, like the rest of the surahs.

We still have the basmalah as a mu'mal majrur (a word governed by a preposition, here the bi- of "bi-smi"), because every noun in the genitive governed by the bi- is in a state of being governed (mu'mal) in every case. And what is meant by "governed"? It means that it needs a governing element ('amil) which is omitted. For this reason the author of the poem "al-Jumal" said:

A jarr (preposition) must have a connection
To a verb, or to its meaning, such as "murtaqi" (ascending).

The basmalah is governed by an omitted governing element. I have now given you a rule: what is it? Every noun in the genitive needs a governing element. So where is the governing element of ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾? We say: the governing element is omitted, and it is estimated as a verb, delayed, and suitable to the context. It is estimated as a verb, second, delayed, and suitable to the context. I want to read, so I say: "In the name of Allah." Estimate the governing element. I read. The estimation is: "In the name of Allah I read."

If you ask: Why do we estimate it as a verb and not as a noun, so that we say: "In the name of Allah is my recitation"?

The answer: The basic principle in governing is verbs. For this reason you will not find a noun acting as a governing element except under conditions. We are now giving you the rules, my brothers. We say we estimated it as a verb for this reason: because the basic principle in governing, or in operating, is that it be a verb, and the evidence for that is that no noun acts as a governing element except under conditions.

Why did we estimate it as delayed and not say: "I read in the name of Allah"? For two benefits:

The first benefit: seeking blessing by beginning speech with the name of Allah.

The second: restriction (hasr), meaning: in the name of Allah and not in the name of anyone else. When the object precedes the governing element, that is evidence of restriction, meaning exclusivity. So it is as if the reader says: "In the name of Allah I read, not in the name of another."

Why did we estimate it as a suitable verb? Because it is more indicative of the intended meaning. For example, when we want to read, we say: the estimation is "In the name of Allah I read."

If someone says: Why don't we say "In the name of Allah I begin"?

We say: Because the word "I begin" is suitable for every action one begins with, whereas when you say "I read," it becomes specific, and it is more indicative of the intended meaning. This is the explanation of the grammatical analysis of ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ whenever it comes to you.

When food is served, you say "In the name of Allah." How do we estimate it?

* Students: "In the name of Allah I eat."
* The Shaykh: "I eat"? No, there is something more specific: "I am having lunch," or "I eat the lunch," because it is more specific.

If you want to drink, you say: "In the name of Allah, I drink." If you want to enter the mosque, you say: "In the name of Allah, I enter," and so on.

As for our saying "In the name of Allah," the intended meaning is every name of Allah. We take it to be general because a singular noun when made genitive by an annexed noun becomes general. That is: I begin with every name of Allah's names. "The Most Merciful" means: possessor of vast mercy. "The Especially Merciful" means: possessor of mercy specific to the believers, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And ever is He to the believers Merciful﴾ [al-Ahzab 43].

﴿Ha-Mim﴾. The commentator (al-Mufassir) said: "Allah knows best what He intends by it." ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ are two letters of the alphabet: one is ha', and the second is mim. They have no grammatical inflection.

Do they have a meaning? The author, the commentator, says: "Allah knows best what He intends by it." So we do not know whether they have a meaning or not, nor what is meant by meaning. So what is our position on this? Delegation (tafwid): Allah knows best. The same is said of every disjointed letter (huruf muqatta'ah) with which a surah begins. Does any other than "Ha-Mim" have it? Yes: Alif-Lam-Mim, Alif-Lam-Ra, Nun, Qaf, Sad, and the like.

So the author, may Allah have mercy on him, says: "What is it to us to interpret it? Allah knows best what He intends by it. Perhaps He intended a meaning, perhaps He did not intend a meaning, perhaps He intended a meaning indicated by the surah, and perhaps He intended another meaning."

But this view is weak. The correct view is to say: it has no meaning. "It has no meaning" does not mean that it is superfluous and without benefit. No, it has no meaning intrinsically. The evidence is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an﴾ [Yusuf 2], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾ [al-Zukhruf 3], and His saying: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic language﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 193–195]. Three verses. Has the Arabic language had disjointed letters placed in it that have a meaning? No. The Arabic language has alphabetic letters placed in it so that speech may be composed from them, and in the Arabic language they are twenty-eight letters.

When you read on the board: alif, ba', ta', tha', jim, ha', kha', what do they mean? They have no meaning. They are only letters from which words are formed. If that is so, and the Noble Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language, then we affirm that these letters have no meaning. How do we affirm it? I seek refuge in Allah! And if Allah intended something by them? We say: He could not intend something by them while it was revealed in the Arabic language, and the Arabic language does not give these alphabetic letters a meaning. We affirm this on the basis of His saying: ﴿Arabic﴾.

The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Ta-Ha [1] We have not sent down the Qur'an to you that you be distressed﴾ [Ta-Ha 1–2]. Is "Ta-Ha" one of the names of the Messenger? No. "Ta-Ha" is like "Alif-Lam-Ra" and like "Ha-Mim": two alphabetic letters with no meaning. If someone says: "We have not sent down to you," the address is to him; we say: then let "Nun" be one of the names of the Messenger, because Allah said: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe [2] You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman﴾ [al-Qalam 1–2], and no one holds that.

If someone says: What is the benefit of these alphabetic letters if they have no meaning in themselves?

I say: The benefit has been pointed out by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah and others among the scholars who preceded and followed him. The benefit is to draw attention to the fact that this noble Qur'an, which people were unable to produce a like of, did not come with new letters, so that people could object and say: "These are letters we do not know, they are new." The noble Qur'an came with letters familiar to those it addressed, and yet it rendered them powerless. Shaykh al-Islam and others said: For this reason you will hardly find a surah that opens with these alphabetic letters without finding, after them, a mention of the Qur'an.

Tell me, my brother, mention three surahs that open with the alphabetic letters and have a mention of the Qur'an after them.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿Alif Lam Mim. That is the Book﴾ [al-Baqarah 1-2]. That is one.
* Student: Maryam.
* Shaykh: Maryam does not contain a mention of the Qur'an. Do not go around in circles, because the Book (...). Who knows the second?
* Student: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. That is the Book, there is no doubt in it﴾.
* Shaykh: Al-Baqarah?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: The brother has mentioned it.
* Student: ﴿Ta Ha. We did not send down to you the Qur'an that you be distressed﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿Ta Ha. We did not send down to you the Qur'an that you be distressed﴾.
* Student: These are the grouped surahs beginning with ﴿Ha Mim﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, correct: ﴿Ha Mim. By the clear Book﴾. The rest can be measured by this. There are a few surahs in which there is no mention of the Qur'an, but there is something specific to the Qur'an, such as the knowledge of the unseen, like: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land﴾ [al-Rum 1-3]. This one has no mention of the Qur'an, but there is something specific to the Qur'an in it, which is knowledge of the unseen in the future.

We say: What is the correct tafsir (exegesis) of ﴿Ha Mim﴾?

We say: It has no meaning in and of itself, but it has a purpose. This which we have established is what Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, the imam of the mufassirin (exegetes) of his time, reported, and Ibn Kathir transmitted it from him in his tafsir.

He said: ﴿And by the clear Book﴾. ﴿And by the Book﴾: the waw is a particle of oath. He explained it as the Qur'an, because Allah the Exalted named the Qur'an a book, saying: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. That is the Book﴾. It was called a book because it was written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and because it was written in the scrolls in the hands of the noble, righteous scribes, and because it was written in the copies that are in our hands. Three aspects: it was written in the Preserved Tablet; second, in the scrolls of the angels; third, in our scrolls that are in our hands.

As for His saying ﴿al-Mubin﴾ (the clear), the commentator says: (the one that makes clear the path of guidance and what is needed of the Sharia). ﴿al-Mubin﴾ is from abana al-shay', meaning he made it manifest. So the meaning of its being clear is that it is manifest and clarifies the truth, indeed everything that people need. ﴿al-Mubin﴾ from (abana), i.e., made manifest; meaning that the Qur'an makes manifest everything people need in their religion and their worldly affairs.

It was said: What is meant by ﴿al-Mubin﴾ is "the clear" (al-bayyin).

Which is more general: "the clear" (al-bayyin), or "the one that makes clear the thing" (al-mubayyin)? The more general is that it is manifest of the truth, because it does not make the truth manifest unless it is itself manifest. On this basis, explain al-mubin as "the one that makes manifest." If you explain it as both, there is no harm, and you say: it is clear and makes clear. Because a word, if it admits two meanings (and this is a rule): when a word admits two meanings that do not contradict each other and neither is preferred over the other, it is taken to mean both. Let me repeat the rule a second time: if a word admits two equal meanings that do not contradict each other, it is taken to mean both together.

﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾. ﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾: the commentator says: (We brought the Book into existence as ﴿an Arabic Qur'an﴾, in the language of the Arabs), ﴿so that you﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿might reason﴾, i.e., understand its meanings.

His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: ﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾. The pronoun, the subject pronoun, refers to Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the object pronoun refers to the Qur'an. The meaning of ﴿We have made it﴾, according to the author's statement, is "We brought it into existence as an Arabic Qur'an." The correct meaning is: We rendered it an Arabic Qur'an, i.e., We rendered it in the language of the Arabs.

﴿So that you might reason﴾, i.e., understand. The address in His words ﴿so that you﴾, according to the words of the mufassir, refers to the people of Makkah. The correct view is that it refers to all the Arabs, because the Arabs are the people of Makkah and others. So the meaning is: We rendered it in the language of the Arabs so that you, O Arabs, may understand it. That concludes the discussion of the verses in terms of wording.

The meaning: Allah the Exalted swore by the Qur'an that He made it in the Arabic language so that it may be understood. From these verses several benefits are derived. Among them: the permissibility of swearing even when the one swearing is already confirmed to be truthful without an oath, meaning that it is permissible for a person to swear about a matter even though his word is accepted in any case.

The basis for this: Allah the Exalted swore, and His word is accepted in every case, and He is truthful without oath.

From this arises the question: how does Allah the Exalted swear about a matter when He is truthful without oath?

We say: for two benefits. The first benefit: to show the importance of this matter, that it is worthy to be sworn about.

The second: that swearing is one of the eloquent features of speech in the Arabic language. If it is one of the eloquent features of speech, and the Qur'an was revealed in what? In the Arabic language, then this conforms to the style of the Arabic language.

An objection arises against this: how did Allah swear by the Qur'an, when it is not permissible to swear by other than Allah?

The answer: the Qur'an is an attribute of Allah, because it is the speech of Allah, and oaths are permissible by Allah and by one of His attributes. So the objection is removed. Have you understood now?

What is the objection that arises? How can Allah swear by the Qur'an when an oath is only by Allah the Exalted?

The answer: it is permissible to swear by the attributes of Allah the Exalted, because they are magnified, and the Qur'an is one of the attributes of Allah, since it is the speech of Allah the Exalted.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the demonstration of the greatness of the Qur'an, because Allah swears only by a great thing. Indeed, the oath itself, as the one who explained it said, is the affirmation of a matter by mentioning something magnified in a specific form by one of the particles of oath. Master the definition of oath: the affirmation of a matter by mentioning something magnified, in a specific form, by one of the particles of oath. The particles of oath are three: waw, ba', and ta'.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Qur'an is mubin, i.e., makes manifest. Makes manifest what? It makes manifest the truth and everything people need. Indeed, it makes manifest even falsehood; it clarifies falsehood and warns against it. Indeed, it is an exposition of everything. Everything: the Qur'an clarifies it. Everything? Yes, everything.

If someone says: Allah the Exalted mentioned things in which there is no room for knowledge; where is their clarification?

We say: their clarification is in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 11], concerning what relates to the attributes; because clarifying them in detail is something the intellects cannot bear, so it was of wisdom not to detail them. Otherwise, it is a clarification of everything.

It is mentioned that one of the scholars was in a restaurant, and near him was a Christian man. The Christian seized the opportunity to pose a question to this scholar as a challenge. He came to him and said: O Shaykh. He said: Yes, what do you want? He said: Your book says: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an exposition of all things﴾ [al-Nahl 89]. So how do we make this salṭa? Do you know the salṭa? It seems some of you do not know it.

* Student: Known.
* Shaykh: Known? What is it? In any case, the salṭa is the zaltah, and the sin and the zay alternate, meaning each one substitutes for the other.

How do we make this salṭa? Where is this in the Qur'an? The Muslim scholar was clever, and he said: It is in the Qur'an, it exists, how to make it. He said: Where? So he called the cook and said: Come here. How did you make this? The cook began explaining to him. He said: This is how it is in the Qur'an. He said: How? He said: Allah said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl 43]. So He referred us, regarding what we do not know, to someone who knows. This is clarification. We were not perplexed now; we were not perplexed about knowing how this salṭa is made.

If someone said to us: The Qur'an is an exposition of everything; how do we make this telephone? Is there in the Qur'an a description of its manufacture? How do we make this telephone? Where is its mention in the Qur'an?

We say: Praise be to Allah, Allah the Exalted referred us to asking the one who knows if we do not know, and this is clarification. He did not leave us bewildered.

So ﴿and by the clear Book﴾: in this verse is evidence that the Qur'an clarifies everything. But, O brothers, the Qur'an requires reflection (tadabbur); without reflection you cannot be guided. Know that whenever you go deeper and more profoundly into reflecting on the Qur'an, Allah opens for you doors of knowledge that were not there before, and you begin to derive from a single verse rulings that others do not derive. So be eager for reflection. The remaining benefits, Allah willing, will come in the next lesson, Allah the Exalted willing.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. The context of the verses in which ﴿ask the people of remembrance﴾ appears was in regard to the mission of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Is it valid to cite them as evidence for...?
* Shaykh: In generality, yes, it is valid, because the lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the cause.
* Student: Shaykh, some students of knowledge always derive from the verses?
* Shaykh: Fine, but on condition that the derivation is something the verse can bear. Some people derive from verses what the verses cannot bear. Have you seen, when the first arrival of humans on the moon happened, and perhaps it happened before most of you distinguished yourselves (most of you are young, praise be to Allah). When this event occurred and they said humans had reached the moon, took a sample from it, brought it to earth, and claimed it was from the moon, black stones we saw. Do you know what people said? They said: This is in the Qur'an. Listen, my son: in what place? He said: Allah said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [al-Rahman 33]; i.e., with knowledge. And these people reached the regions of the heavens by what? By knowledge. They said: This verse indicates this.

But this interpretation is forbidden, and speaking about Allah, and lying about Allah. The verse is in the context of challenge: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass﴾. Can Allah the Exalted challenge anyone with what they are able to do? It is impossible. Challenge means that the one addressed is unable. This is one point.

Second: the verse ﴿if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth﴾ begins with the heavens. Can these people pass beyond the regions of the heavens? It is impossible. If the best messenger among humans and the best messenger among angels did not enter the lowest heaven except by request for opening and permission, how can these people? If they pass through the regions of the earth, they do not pass through the regions of the heavens.

Third: Allah the Exalted said after His words ﴿you will not pass except with authority﴾: ﴿There will be sent against you a flame of fire and molten copper, and you will not be victorious﴾ [al-Rahman 35]. Has a flame of fire and copper been sent upon these people? No. So interpreting the Qur'an by what it cannot bear is forbidden, because the interpreter bears witness that Allah meant such-and-such.

Like the saying of some: ﴿And you see the mountains, you think them rigid, but they pass as the passing of clouds﴾ [al-Naml 88]. He said: This is clear evidence that the earth revolves. This matter has caused a great dispute: does the earth revolve or not? It revolves or it does not. I mean I am relating the disagreement. Much conflict arose over it, and pamphlets and small treatises were written in newspapers, in denial and in support. Then this man who considers himself learned came and said: This is in the Qur'an: ﴿And you see the mountains, you think them rigid, but they pass as the passing of clouds﴾. It was said to him: This is the Day of Resurrection. He said: On the Day of Resurrection one cannot see a thing except as it truly is; he does not see it other than its reality. So he was answered: Have you not read the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾ [al-Hajj 1-2]. Look at ﴿you see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾; this is seeing a thing other than its reality, and it is possible. So the verse ﴿you see the mountains, you think them rigid﴾: when? On the Day of Resurrection; ﴿and they pass as the passing of clouds﴾, because they will become dust scattered.

This is also an error, and burdening the Qur'an with what it cannot bear.

* Student: Is there in the Qur'an any word that is not Arabic?
* Shaykh: No, not at all. Everything in the Qur'an is Arabic, but some of it is of the core of the Arabic language, and some of it is arabized (mu'arrab), its origin is non-Arabic but it was arabized. And when it was arabized, it became Arabic. Have you seen that if you take citizenship in a country, are you of them or not? You are of them, though originally you are from others. So there is nothing in the Qur'an that is not Arabic.

If someone says: There is sundus, istabraq, and the like? The answer: These were arabized and became part of the speech of the Arabs.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, the verses in which Allah swears by the star, the moon, and the sun: some explain that Allah swears by whatever He wills, but the created being swears only by Allah. Is this interpretation correct?
* Shaykh: This is correct. Allah may swear by whatever He wills of His creation, and it is not for us to swear except by Him.
* Student: And for us in this verse...
* Shaykh: No, this verse is an oath by the attributes of Allah; there is no problem with it.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. ﴿Ha Mim. By the clear Book. Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you might reason. And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise. Shall We then turn away from you the reminder, because you are a transgressing people? And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples. And there did not come to them a prophet except that they used to mock him. So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, and the example of the former peoples has passed﴾ [al-Zukhruf 1-8].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Ha Mim. By the clear Book﴾. What is the preferred view regarding ﴿Ha Mim﴾?
* Student: That it has no specific meaning, and that it has a purpose: to show the inimitability of the Qur'an.
* Shaykh: The question: what is the preferred view regarding it?
* Student: It has no meaning.
* Shaykh: It has no meaning in and of itself. What is the evidence that it has no meaning in and of itself?
* Student: Because Allah addressed us with the Qur'an, which was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue, and the Arabs did not use the letters to mean a specific thing.
* Shaykh: Because Allah revealed the Qur'an in a clear Arabic tongue, and these alphabetic letters have no meaning in the Arabic language. Correct.
* Student: Yes indeed.
* Shaykh: And this is the view of Mujahid ibn Jabr, may Allah have mercy on him, the imam of the mufassirin among the Successors.

What is the meaning of the waw in His saying ﴿And by the clear Book﴾?
* Student: The waw is for conjunction.
* Shaykh: For conjunction? Wrong.
* Student: For oath.
* Shaykh: The waw is for oath. An oath requires one who swears, a thing sworn by, and a thing sworn about. Who is the one swearing?
* Student: The one swearing is Allah the Exalted.
* Shaykh: The one swearing is Allah. And the thing sworn by?
* Student: The Book.
* Shaykh: The Book, which is the Qur'an. And the thing sworn about?
* Student: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾.
* Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾. May Allah bless you. The particles of oath?

Student: The particles of oath are the waw, the ba', and the ta'.

Shaykh: Three: the waw, the ba', and the ta'. Give an example of the waw.

Student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By the Clear Book﴾.

Shaykh: Yes, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By the Clear Book﴾. The waw is the one most used in oaths. The ba'?

Student: Like the speaker's saying, as came in the hadiths: "By Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad"[[Among what al-Bukhari (2615) and Muslim (2469 / 127) narrated, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A silk garment was presented to the Prophet ﷺ, and he used to forbid silk, so the people marvelled at it. He said: "By Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this."]].

Shaykh: ("By the One who..."), I do not mean that; I mean the ba'.

Student: Like the speaker's saying: "By Allah, what I told you is true."

Shaykh: Yes, I swear by Allah that this is true. The ta'?

Student: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By Allah, you almost led me astray﴾ [al-Saffat 56].

Shaykh: ﴿He said: By Allah, you almost led me astray﴾, correct. What is the meaning of ﴿al-Mubin﴾?

Student: The one that makes manifest the truth and falsehood and everything.

Shaykh: The one that clarifies everything that needs clarification in matters of religion and worldly affairs. Correct. Is there evidence in the Qur'an for what you have just said?

Student: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾.

Shaykh: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾. May Allah bless you.

Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand﴾. We have discussed this. ﴿Made it﴾?

Student: We made it (ṣayyaranāhu, "We rendered it").

Shaykh: We rendered it. And what is the meaning of ﴿We made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾?

Student: That is: We rendered it in the Arabic language.

Shaykh: That is: We rendered it in the Arabic language. Correct. As for His saying: ﴿that you may understand﴾, who can explain to us the meaning of (la'alla, "that perhaps")?

Student: The Arabs.

Shaykh: No, (la'alla) means what?

Student: Hope.

Shaykh: Wrong.

Student: Here (la'alla) is meant to express causation.

Shaykh: (La'alla) indicates causation, meaning: for the sake of?

Student: That you may understand.

Shaykh: That you may understand. Good. And what is meant by ʿaql (understanding/reason) here?

Student: It means the intellect of right judgment and comprehension.

Shaykh: No. In ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand﴾, it means the intellect of comprehension: so that you may comprehend it.

A similar verse is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, to make clear to them﴾ [Ibrahim 4].

From the benefits of this verse: this Qur'an was made of the same letters from which the Arabs compose their speech, yet it defeated them.

Among the benefits: it is permissible to emphasize a report with an oath, even if the one reporting cannot be suspected of lying. The reason: Allah, Exalted is He, swore, though His speech cannot admit falsehood, but this is because of the importance of what is sworn about.

Among them: the excellence and greatness of the noble Qur'an, since Allah swore by it, and one swears only by something magnified.

Among them: the noble Qur'an is written. It is written in the Preserved Tablet, written in the scrolls in the hands of the angels, and written in the scrolls that are in our hands.

Among them: the noble Qur'an is clarifying for everything that needs clarification, by His saying: ﴿al-Mubin﴾. But is this clarity attained by everyone? Listen to the answer: No, it is not attained by everyone. Among people are those who understand many things from the Qur'an, among them those below that level, and among them those who understand nothing. The categories are three: among people is one whom Allah opens up so that he derives from a single verse dozens of rulings, among them those below that level, and among them those who understand nothing.

This is why 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked: "Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, entrust you with anything? He said: No, by the One who split the grain and created the soul, he entrusted us with nothing except an understanding that Allah gives to whomever He wills in the Qur'an, and what is in this scroll"[[Al-Bukhari (111) narrated with his chain from Abu Juhayfa, who said: I said to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: Do you have a book? He said: No, except the Book of Allah, or an understanding given to a Muslim man, or what is in this scroll. I said: What is in this scroll? He said: The blood-money, the ransoming of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever.]]. 'Ali was asked about this because it was rumoured in his time that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, had entrusted him with the caliphate and said: "You are the caliph after me." So he, may Allah be pleased with him, made clear that this had not happened.

The point from this report is his words: "except an understanding that Allah gives to whichever of His servants He wills." That is why, when some scholars speak on a verse deriving its benefits, they bring wondrous things. Among the most eloquent things I have read is what was granted to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, and his student Ibn al-Qayyim, for Allah opened up to them an understanding of the Qur'an that was not granted to others.

Among people is one whose understanding is below that, but in degrees. And among people is one who understands nothing. The evidence for the last is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Book except for wishful fancies﴾ [al-Baqara 78], meaning: except recitation. (Amaniyy is the plural of umniyya.) From this is the poet's saying about the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him:

He longed for the Book of Allah at the start of his night
and at its end he met the death of the watering places.

(Tamanna kitab Allah): what does it mean? It means he recited the Book of Allah, because the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed as a martyr in his house while he was performing night prayer and reciting the Qur'an.

Does the one who does not understand detract from the Qur'an being an explanation of all things? No, because the Qur'an in itself is an explanation of all things, just as the coward who holds a sharp sword does not strike with it, and this is no fault in the sword.

From the benefits of this noble verse: the Qur'an is created (ḥādith), meaning it is by the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾. Allah is able to make it in another language, but He rendered it in Arabic. And it is known that the Arabs are created, or eternal? Created. So what was sent down in their language is created. This is the truth: that the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is created, in the sense that He speaks whenever He wills; whenever He wills He speaks, and whenever He wills He does not speak, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "And He was silent about some things out of mercy for you, not forgetfulness"[[Narrated by al-Daraqutni in his Sunan (4396), and Ibn al-Muqri in his Mu'jam (471), with the wording of the latter, from the hadith of Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

It is among the creed of Ahl al-Sunna wal-Jama'a that Allah speaks with real speech whenever He wills, about whatever He wills, in whatever manner He wills.

We have said: the speech of Allah Exalted is created, meaning that He brings into existence from His speech whatever He wills. And among the principles of Ahl al-Sunna wal-Jama'a is that Allah, Exalted is He, speaks with real speech whenever He wills, about whatever He wills, in whatever manner He wills.

Do you not know that the Ash'aris, who ascribe themselves to Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, say: Allah does not speak whenever He wills? Never. Why? They say: because speech is a meaning subsisting in His essence, eternal, but He produces sounds that He creates whenever He wills, which are then heard. They therefore hold that speech is not tied to His will. By Allah, which of these two is more perfect: one who speaks by his will, whenever and however he wills, or one who cannot do this? The first. But their innovation insisted that they say (...). Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote a book he named al-Tis'iniyya, in which he demonstrated the falsehood of this view in ninety aspects. May Allah have mercy on him and reward him on behalf of the Ummah of Muhammad with good.

From the benefits of this verse: that the Qur'an being in the Arabic language is a great honour for the Arabs, that the noble Qur'an was revealed in our language; by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾.

If someone says: this is tribal partisanship and zeal for the Arabs, and the atheist Arabs take pride in it, what is the answer? This is a difficulty, for atheist Arabs who build loyalty and disavowal upon Arabic dictionaries take pride in this.

We say: whoever is a disbeliever has no honour, even if he is of pure Arab stock. The proof: Abu Lahab, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, about whom Allah revealed an entire surah that is recited in prayer, in the evening, and everywhere the Qur'an is recited until the Day of Resurrection. Is it in his praise or his censure? In his censure, and he is of pure Arab stock, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ. So Arabness benefits nothing alongside disbelief. But when religion and worldly life are combined, how good are religion and worldly life when they are joined, when one becomes a Muslim and an Arab.

From the benefits of this noble verse: the proof is not established except by understanding; the proof is not established upon the servants unless they understand it, by His saying: ﴿that you may understand﴾, and "intellect" here means understanding. So if the Qur'an were recited to a non-Arabic-speaking man who does not know its meaning, and he were not told: this is the speech of Allah, then there is no established proof. This is supported by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, to make clear to them﴾ [Ibrahim 4]. Listen, O man, have you understood now? This is a great matter: the proof is not established upon the servants except by understanding it and knowing its meaning. Otherwise, what proof is there in a man speaking words we do not understand? There is no proof. Therefore, if a non-Arab stood before us, while we are Arabs who do not know his language, and spoke in the most eloquent form of his language, would we understand anything? Never. So understanding of the proof is necessary.

If someone says: what do you say about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿that I may warn you by it, and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am 19], and He did not say: "and whoever understands it"?

The answer: we say: ﴿whoever it reaches﴾ is restricted by other texts indicating that understanding is necessary; or it is said: ﴿whoever it reaches﴾ means among the Arabs who understand it...

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 43, verse 4:

He said: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise.﴾ [az-Zukhruf 4] (Innahu) The pronoun refers to ﴿the Clear Book﴾, which is the Quran.

﴿In the Mother of the Book﴾ is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), and it is called "mother" because it is the reference for everything that is written after it. Writing is of several kinds; the great, general, all-encompassing writing is what is written in the Preserved Tablet.

﴿With Us﴾ means "with Us," and the adverbial phrase here is a circumstantial qualifier of ﴿the Mother of the Book﴾. The meaning is that what is with Allah in this verse is the Mother of the Book, i.e., the Preserved Tablet with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is protected from alteration and change because it is the Mother of the Book.

As for the books that the angels bring, there is alteration and change in them, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [ar-Ra'd 39].

﴿Exalted﴾ means possessing loftiness, and ﴿wise﴾ means possessing judgment and wisdom. These are two great attributes of the Noble Quran, with which Allah described Himself. (ʿAliyy) carries the meaning of "high" but is more emphatic, because ʿaliyy is on the pattern faʿīl, an adjective of quality (ṣifah mushabbahah), and the adjective of quality indicates permanence and continuity.

﴿Wise﴾ means possessing judgment and wisdom. So the Quran is judging (ḥākim) and the Quran contains wisdom. The meaning of our saying "judging" is that it is the reference for judgment, and nothing is judged by other than it. The meaning of "judging" is that it is dominant over all matters, judging over them.

Regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise﴾, is the intended meaning "(innahu)" i.e., its mention, or is the intended meaning the Quran itself in the Preserved Tablet?

* A student: The second.

* Another student: The first.

* The Shaykh: It is possible that the intended meaning of ﴿innahu﴾ is its mention, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 196]. It is well known that the Quran is not in the scriptures of the former peoples, but its mention is in the scriptures of the former peoples.

However, if we reflect, we say: the original principle is that the pronoun refers to the very thing it indicates, and in that case (innahu) means the entire Quran is in the Preserved Tablet.

If someone says: this view is subject to an objection, that the Noble Quran contains words in which Allah speaks of something that has already passed, such as the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of the one who argues with you﴾ [al-Mujadila 1]. Is this report after the argument or before it?

* Students: After.

* The Shaykh: Good. The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when you set out in the morning from your family to settle the believers at their positions for battle﴾ [Ali 'Imran 121], referring to the Battle of Uhud, ﴿you set out﴾ meaning you went out in the morning. Is this report given after the occurrence of what is reported, or before it?

* Students: Before.

* Other students: After.

* The Shaykh: O Allah, open [understanding] for us. ﴿When you set out in the morning from your family to settle the believers at their positions for battle﴾.

* The students: After.

* The Shaykh: ﴿When you set out﴾: is this report now, before he went out, or after he had gone out?

* The students: After.

* The Shaykh: After he had gone out, because (ghada) is a past-tense verb, ﴿when you set out﴾. Here a difficulty arises: it is said, how could Allah speak in the Preserved Tablet about something that happened before the verse was revealed?

It is answered: there is no difficulty. The answer is that Allah wrote this in the Preserved Tablet because of His knowledge that it would occur, and then He revealed it after its occurrence, just as cosmic events are written in the Preserved Tablet because of His, the Exalted's, knowledge that they will occur, and then they come to be when Allah wills them to be.

Before that, I used to prefer, indeed I used to say, that it is necessary that what is in the Preserved Tablet is not the Quran itself, but the mention of the Quran; that is, that a Quran will be sent down to this Ummah. They cited as evidence for this the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And indeed it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 196], and what is in the scriptures of the former peoples is undoubtedly the mention of the Quran, relying on verses like those I mentioned to you: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of the one who argues with you concerning her husband﴾ and His saying: ﴿And when you set out﴾. Until I came upon a statement of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, which clarified what I mentioned to you recently: that there is no obstacle to its being written in the Preserved Tablet in the past tense, because Allah knew that it would be and that He would send down this verse after it has occurred.

On this basis, it became clear to me that what is in the Preserved Tablet is the Quran, based on the apparent meaning of the verses: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Quran, in a Preserved Tablet﴾ [al-Buruj 21, 22]. All praise is due to Allah who opened this for me, and may Allah reward Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah with goodness. This shows that no person, whoever he may be, can avoid being subject to deficiency.

As for His saying: ﴿exalted and wise﴾, we have said: its meaning is wisdom and judgment.

* We take the benefits of the verse:

* Among the benefits of the verse: Allah the Blessed and Exalted's care for this Quran, and this indicates its nobility (...), in that He placed it with Him in the Mother of the Book.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that the Quran is high, indeed exalted, and this indicates that whoever holds fast to this Quran will have loftiness, as in the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are superior, and Allah is with you﴾ [Muhammad 35]. So we say: the Quran is exalted, and whoever holds to it will have loftiness.

The reality bears witness to this: when the Islamic Ummah held fast to Islam, it had loftiness and dominance, and it ruled the eastern and western parts of the earth. When it became lax, cowardly, disputatious and hateful, the situation reversed; it came to have humiliation. Now the Arab nation calls the Jews to peace and repeats this, and extends its hands to Christian states to help them make peace. Why? Because we did not hold fast to the Quran, so we became humiliated, begging our enemies that peace be made between us and them. Is it clear? Answer.

* Students: Yes, it is clear.

* The Shaykh: It is clear, brothers; meaning, if someone said to us (...) in the Quran, and yet people are in humiliation? We say: because we did not hold fast to the Quran. Had we held fast to the Quran, we would have gained for ourselves loftiness, dominance and superiority. But the situation is reversed: now most Muslims pant after the world, turning away from religion. What develops the economy? What brings about luxury? And the like. But what strengthens religion? That is little or nonexistent.

So the word ﴿exalted﴾ is on its apparent meaning and its meaning, but on condition that we hold fast to this Quran.

* Among the benefits of this verse: whoever argues with the Quran is victorious, because the one who possesses loftiness is the Quran. Any person who debates with you, and whose means of persuasion and refutation is the Quran, you will certainly defeat him. But when many of the Ummah turned to the speech of the people of kalam, the empty speech, were they guided to the straight path? No. Did they overcome the enemies? No. The enemies dominated them. Even atheist philosophers came to argue with the practices of the Ash'aris about the falsehood they hold, and say: You, O Ash'aris, and you, O Mu'tazilah, have distorted the texts to what you consider reason, and we too have turned away from the texts to what we consider reason. So these people of innovation argued for their atheism and said: We and you are equal; you distorted and we distorted.

But if we held fast to the Quran, could these philosophers argue with us? They cannot. But read the books of the people of kalam and you will find page after page from which you gain not a single benefit; for this reason it is correct to say: they are the people of kalam, and their speech is (kalam); meaning it is vain speech with no benefit.

Consider his saying, may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him and his family, when the Companions complained to him of the whisperings of Satan they found in their souls, he said: «That is the clear faith» [Muslim 132, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him], and he commanded whoever found these whisperings to seek refuge in Allah and desist: «Let him seek refuge in Allah and desist» [agreed upon; al-Bukhari's wording (3276), and Muslim (134/214), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him]. Two words.

What do the philosophers and the theologians write about this? They write much of what they claim to be rational matters, and it is imaginings. We ask Allah to grant us and you adherence to this Mighty Book and to honour us through it.

* A student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you with goodness, is understanding the Quran according to a person's intelligence or according to his piety toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic?

* The Shaykh: Both. This is why ʿAli... this one asks: is the understanding of the Quran according to comprehension or according to piety?

The answer is both. This is why ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: «Except an understanding that Allah grants to whomever He wills in His Book» [al-Bukhari (111) with his chain from Abu Juhayfah, who said: I said to ʿAli ibn Abi Talib: Do you have a book? He said: No, except the Book of Allah, or an understanding given to a Muslim man... the hadith]. Piety has an effect on understanding the Noble Quran. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17], and He said of the Quran: ﴿A guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2].

* A student: Which is the preponderant view on whether the Quran has one descent or two descents, i.e., that it descended to the lowest heaven first, and after that descended?

* The Shaykh: No, the apparent view is that it is one descent. It descended from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; He spoke it, Glorified and Exalted is He, then Jibril heard it and descended with it.

* A student: Shaykh, you mentioned, may Allah preserve you, that you found a benefit from Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah; where did you find it?

* The Shaykh: The apparent place is in the Fatawa.

* A student: Shaykh, your saying that proof is not established except through understanding: does it follow from this, may Allah preserve you, that the grave-worshippers who have not understood the matter of worship properly, and who read the Quran, are excused by that? Because some say: proof is established by the existence of the Book and the Sunnah.

* The Shaykh: These are negligent; that is, the truth is presented to them but they do not accept it. But suppose that there are people far from guidance and knowledge who are Muslims, pray, and perform all the acts of Islam, yet are grave-worshippers; proof is not established against these. But most grave-worshippers now, if not all of them, have been told that this is shirk, yet they fell short and said: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾ [az-Zukhruf 22].

* A student: Shaykh, the view that the Quran has one descent: how do we interpret ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ [al-Qadr 1]?

* The Shaykh: Well said. We interpret this as meaning that Allah began sending it down on the Night of Decree.

* A student: The non-Arabs now (...) and insult of the religion (...) against Islam; I say they are (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, they are obstinate; most of them are obstinate. But they denied (...). If people were far from the light of revelation and knowledge, they would be excused; but they are obstinate. For example, you come to the monk and say: your creed is false; he says: No, the Ayatollah said so, the Hujjat-Allah said so, (...). This is an obstinate person.

* A student: Can the Quran be described as originated (ḥadath)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, or "muhdath" (created in time); muhdath, muhdith and hadith all amount to one meaning. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No reminder comes to them from the Most Merciful, newly revealed, except that they turn away from it﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 5]. But notice: do not think that the meaning of "muhdath" is "created"; no, "muhdath" means that Allah spoke it at the time of its descent.

Shaykh Ibn 'Uthaymin, Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim, on surah 43, verse 5:

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you and turn away from you, because you are a people who exceed the limits? (5) And how many a Prophet We sent among the earlier peoples! (6) But no Prophet came to them except that they mocked him. (7) So We destroyed those stronger than these in might, and the example of the earlier peoples has passed on. (8) And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Almighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 5–9].

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you and turn away from you, because you are a people who exceed the limits?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 5]. The hamzah here is interrogative, but it is meant as negation, as is shown by the fact that the mufassir (Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli) afterwards supplied the word "not" (lā). That is: "We will not withhold the Reminder from you by turning away." The meaning is that We cannot leave you without a warning because you are a people who exceed the limits; rather, a warning must be given, just as you say: "I turned away from this, ṣafḥan," meaning: I turned away from it and did not give it any attention. What is meant by this, as I have said, is negation in the form of a rebuke to these people who turned away from what the Prophet ﷺ brought.

The pronoun in His saying "We withhold" (naḍrib) refers to Allah the Exalted. He used the pronoun denoting plurality out of magnification of Allah the Exalted, not to indicate multiplicity, since Allah the Exalted is One with no partner.

The pronoun in His saying ﴿from you﴾ refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh who denied Muhammad ﷺ.

His saying ﴿ṣafḥan﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) of the meaning of the verb "naḍrib" (We withhold), since its meaning is "turning away" (i‘rāḍan).

I think you now understand the general meaning: that they turned away from being reminded and warned. This is the meaning of the verse.

This is what you have heard the Arabs use in their speech. One says: "I turned away from you ṣafḥan," meaning: I did not care for you and did not look at you.

﴿because you are a people who exceed the limits﴾: "an" and "mā" joined to it are in the sense of a verbal noun serving as an object of purpose, i.e. "because you were a people who exceed the limits," so it is causal (taʿlīliyyah).

Al-Isrāf (excess) means going beyond the limit.

Benefits from this verse:

* Allah, blessed and exalted, has not left His servants neglected; rather, He made the truth clear to them, called them to it, and warned them against opposing it, so no one has any excuse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person is excused by ignorance if the message has not reached him.

There are evidences for this, among them the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ [An-Nisa 163], up to His saying: ﴿messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [An-Nisa 165]. Among them is His saying: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger﴾ [Al-Isra 15]. Among them is His saying: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns until He sends in their mother-town a messenger reciting to them Our verses; and We would not destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Qasas 59]. The evidences for this are many.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, no one of this nation hears of me, whether Jew or Christian, and then dies without believing in what I have brought, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire."[[Recorded by Muslim (153/240) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] He said: "No one hears of me."

If someone says: Is it a condition, along with the message reaching a person, that the addressee understands it?

The answer: Yes, this is a condition, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to make clear to them﴾ [Ibrahim 4]. What benefit is there in a messenger who comes to a people who do not know his language, while he does not know theirs? What benefit would be achieved? None. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is too merciful and too wise to punish a people without their understanding what the messengers brought.

There remains the question: if a person is a Muslim but commits acts of shirk without believing them to be shirk, is he judged to be a polytheist?

The answer: No, not until the proof is established against him. When the proof is established against him, then we judge him to be a polytheist.

If someone says: A man in the forests, far from the cities and far from civilization, but he belongs to a religion of disbelief; is he excused?

The answer: As for the rulings of this world, he is not excused; that is, we treat him as a disbeliever, because he does not adhere to the religion of Islam, unlike the first case. We treat him in this world as a disbeliever. As for the Hereafter, his affair is with Allah the Exalted, and we do not know what will become of him. It has been related in a hadith that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will send messengers to the People of the Interval (ahl al-fatrah) to test them: whoever obeys enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys enters the Fire.[[Ahmad (16301) and Ibn Hibban (7357), the wording being his, narrated from al-Aswad ibn Sari‘, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who said: "Four will present arguments on the Day of Resurrection: a deaf man, a fool, an aged man, and a man who died in the interval. As for the deaf man, he will say: 'O Lord, Islam has come, and I hear nothing.' As for the fool, he will say: 'Lord, Islam has come while the boys were pelting me with dung.' As for the aged man, he will say: 'Lord, Islam has come and I do not understand.' As for the one who died in the interval, he will say: 'Lord, no messenger came to me from You.' So He will take their covenants that they will obey Him, and He will send to them a messenger saying: 'Enter the Fire.' He said: 'By Him in whose hand my soul is, if they entered it, it would be cool and safe for them.'" Also narrated by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in his Musnad (514) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who said: "Four will all present to Allah an argument and an excuse: a man who died in the interval, a man who died in old age, a man who was mentally impaired, and a man who was deaf and mute. Allah will say to them: 'I am sending a messenger to you, so obey him.' He will come to them and kindle a fire for them, and say: 'Plunge into it.' Whoever plunges into it, it will be cool and safe for him, and whoever does not plunge into it, the word of punishment will be due against him."]]

If someone says: According to your view, it follows that the Hereafter is an abode of obligation, since you say that Allah sends a messenger who tests them; does it follow that the Hereafter is an abode of obligation?

The answer: Yes, we accept this, and the Qur'an has indicated that the Hereafter is an abode of obligation. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿On the Day when the shin is uncovered and they are called to prostration, but they will not be able. Their eyes will be humbled; humiliation will cover them, and they used to be called to prostration while they were sound﴾ [Al-Qalam 42–43]. Here they were obligated to prostrate, although the Hereafter is not in origin an abode of obligation, but people may be obligated therein.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the rulings of Allah the Mighty and Majestic are founded on causes appropriate to the ruling, and this is part of the requirement of His wisdom. You will not find a ruling except that it has a wisdom. But does it follow that its wisdom is known to us?

The answer: No, because our understanding and intellects are too limited to encompass the knowledge of the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. But we know that He does not decree anything, whether by decree or by law, except that it has a wisdom. If you see that Allah the Mighty and Majestic has ruled a matter in the Book or the Sunnah, do not seek a substitute for it, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ [Al-Ahzab 36]. When the Mother of the Believers, 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, was asked about a menstruating woman who makes up fasting but not prayer, she said: "This used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fasts but not commanded to make up the prayers."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321), and Muslim, the wording being his (335/69), from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]

Then the Most High said: ﴿And how many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 6]. (Kam) here is *khabariyya* (a term for "kam" used to indicate a large quantity), and what governs it is what follows it: ﴿We sent﴾. Irsal (sending) means revelation to a human being of a law, with a command to convey it.

His saying ﴿a prophet﴾ explains (kam). The intended meaning here is the messenger, because He said ﴿how many a prophet We sent﴾, and the word "nabi" (prophet) is often applied to the messenger in the Noble Qur'an, as in ﴿Indeed, he was a man of truth, a prophet﴾ [Maryam 41], and similar verses. The intended meaning is the messenger.

﴿Among the earlier peoples﴾ means those who came before this nation.

(﴿And no prophet came to them﴾ ... ) (﴿And no﴾ ... ﴿came to them﴾) The author supplied (kana, "was"), because the matter has already passed. Had the wording followed the sequence of the speech, ﴿and no prophet comes to them﴾, it would refer to the future. Therefore the commentator supplied (kana), and this shows the depth of the commentator's knowledge.

However, it is better than that to say: there is no need for supplying anything, because when there is a choice between a sentence containing an implied element and one without, the default is that there is no implied element. So we say: the verse remains on its apparent meaning, but it is a narration of the present situation (*hikayat al-hal*, the vivid present); that is, as if the past were present now, and this is more forceful in warning the Quraysh against opposition.

Why did the author supply (kana)? Because the Qur'an speaks of something that has passed, so we must supply a past verb. We say: there is no need for supplying, and the verse came in the context of the present (imperfect) verb, which indicates the future, as a narration of the situation, as if the matter were happening now. This is more forceful in warning the Quraysh and cautioning them.

﴿And no prophet comes to them﴾: the (min) here is grammatically superfluous (*za'ida i'raban*) but semantically meaningful. It is superfluous grammatically in the sense that if it were removed from the context, the sentence would be complete without it. If the verse read: "And no prophet comes to them", would the sentence be sound or not?

* Student: It is sound.

* The Shaykh: But (min) came as an addition for a benefit. What is the benefit?

The scholars of rhetoric and grammar say that the addition of a word, i.e. a particle, in a sentence indicates emphasis. Accordingly, every superfluous word in the Qur'an in terms of grammar carries a meaning.

﴿And no prophet came to them but that they used to mock him﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 7]. Look — and Allah forbid — no prophet came to them but they mocked him. ﴿But that they used to mock him﴾: this is their state; they do not accept him, nor do they remain silent, but they mock. Istihza' (mockery) is ridicule, meaning that they deride them and belittle them, in order to warn people against them.

So consider the mercy of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: He sends the messengers while He knows that these so-called people will confront them with mockery, but as an establishment of the proof.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah the Most High sent a great number of prophets among the earlier peoples. It has come in some hadiths that they were one hundred and twenty-four thousand,[[Ahmad (22288) narrated with his chain from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many were the prophets in number?" He said: "One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand; the messengers among them were three hundred and fifteen, a great number..."]] but Allah knows best, because this requires a sound and explicit proof, and Allah the Most High said: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you; among them are those We have related to you and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78]. It is known that whoever has not been related to us, we cannot know their number.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah the Most High established the proof upon all creation, and this is confirmed by His saying: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir 24].

* And among the benefits of this verse: consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ), by His saying: ﴿And no prophet came to them but that they used to mock him﴾. When the Prophet (ﷺ) knows that the messengers before him were mocked, he is consoled, without doubt. You find this in yourselves: when you are struck by a calamity and others are struck by its like or worse, do you not take comfort in this and the calamity becomes easier for you?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Good, that is correct. And on this Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 39]; meaning that their sharing in the punishment does not lighten the punishment for you, nor does it bring you any consolation, because each one of the people of the Fire — may Allah protect us and you from it — does not see anyone with a lighter punishment than his own. Therefore his grief intensifies — and Allah forbid — when he sees that he is the one with the greatest punishment while he is the least of them.

* And among the benefits of this verse: mocking the messengers is a further burden for them, by His saying: ﴿but that they used to mock him﴾.

Know that mocking the messengers is disbelief, mocking the books is disbelief, and mocking Allah is disbelief. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And if you asked them, they would surely say, "We were only conversing and playing." Say, "Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?" Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief﴾ [At-Tawbah 65–66].

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed concerning one who mocks Allah, His verses, or His messenger, or curses Allah, His book, or His messenger: is his repentance accepted or not? There are two opinions.

The correct view is to make a distinction: if there is evidence of his uprightness and the soundness of his repentance, it is accepted; otherwise, it is not.

This is because the one who mocks, ridicules, or curses has three states:

The first state: that he persists in that. For such a person there is no repentance, and he is to be killed as an apostate.

The second: that we know he has repented sincerely, because he has become upright and his condition has been set right. His repentance is accepted without any difficulty.

The third: that we are in doubt as to whether he is sincere in his repentance or not. Such a person is to be killed, and his affair is left to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. We kill him for his apparent state, because we are not certain that this state has changed to something that would prevent his being killed, so we kill him. As for the Hereafter, his affair is with Allah.

If someone says: mocking Allah and cursing Allah the Mighty and Majestic is a grave sin that cannot be such that the repentance of its perpetrator is accepted?

The answer: read the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic in the same verse: ﴿Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon one faction of you, We will punish another faction﴾ [At-Tawbah 66]; meaning: if We pardon a group because of their repentance, We punish the other group that did not repent. And read the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ [Az-Zumar 53].
