* Student: And with a kasra, it is from mockery.
* Shaykh: From what?
* Student: From mockery.
* Another student: The reverse, Shaykh.
* Shaykh: There is no power nor strength except with Allah.
* Student: "Sukhriyyan" means subjugation.
* Shaykh: Yes. "Sukhriyyan" with a damma on the sin is from?
* Student: From taskhir.
* Shaykh: From taskhir, which is subjugation.
* Student: And with a kasra, from mockery.
* Shaykh: From "sukhriyya," which is mockery.

Which is appropriate here, the damma or the kasra, in the Qur'an?
* Students: The damma.
* Shaykh: The damma, because it is from taskhir. Were it not for this variation among people, livelihoods would be disrupted. If they were all wealthy, who would do the work? Answer me, everyone.
* Students: No one.
* Shaykh: No one would do it, because if he is asked to work, he says: "If you have a thousand riyals, I have two thousand." The same applies to the other attributes. Were it not for this variation, the world would never have been set in order. This is part of the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then there is another wisdom: that through this the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, becomes known, in that He made humankind of one kind, with one set of powers, and yet they differ greatly in what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has given them of wealth and other things. This is a parenthetical statement (...).
... the Mighty and Majestic: (﴿And the mercy of your Lord﴾, meaning: Paradise; ﴿is better than what they accumulate﴾, meaning: in this world).

As for His words, ﴿And the mercy of your Lord﴾, meaning: Paradise. There is also some deficiency in this. "Mercy" is undoubtedly applied to Paradise, as Allah said to it, addressing it: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4850) and Muslim (2846/34), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿As for those whose faces turn black, "Did you disbelieve after your belief? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve." (106) But as for those whose faces turn white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide eternally﴾ [Al Imran 106–107], meaning: Paradise. But it should be said that the mercy of Allah is more general than this. Even Allah's mercy to the servant in guiding him to Islam and faith is better than what they accumulate. So generalization is better than restriction.

* In this verse there are benefits. Among them: the argument against polytheists with falsehood, by His words. What is the evidence?
* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Arguing with the polytheists with falsehood. From where is it derived? Do you not have knowledge?
* Student: His words: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾.
* Shaykh: Wrong.
* Student: His words: ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two towns?"﴾.
* Shaykh: From their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two towns?﴾. The reason is that the Quraysh knew that Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, was the most deserving of people of prophethood, had they believed in it, because he was of the best Arab lineage, and because he was the trustworthy and truthful one. They called him "al-Amin" before he came with prophethood.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the word "qarya" (town) is applied to large cities, indeed to the mother of cities, by His words: ﴿from the two towns, a great one﴾, and by His words in another verse: ﴿And how many a town was stronger in might than your town which expelled you﴾ [Muhammad 13]. Which is the town that expelled him?
* Student: Makkah.
* Shaykh: Makkah. In our custom today, "qarya" is applied to a small town. If you said to the people of a large city, "You are the people of a qarya," they would become furious. But it is said: the Qur'an is between us. "Qarya" is applied even to a large city, because it derives from "qary," which means gathering.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's refutation of them, and clarifying that they are not the ones who distribute the mercy of Allah, by His words: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾.
* Among its benefits: establishing the proof that cannot be disentangled from, that they cannot distribute the mercy of Allah. Is it derived?
* Student: His words: "Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?"
* Shaykh: Wrong.
* Student: His words, the Exalted: ﴿We have distributed among them their livelihood﴾.
* Shaykh: It is derived from His words: ﴿We have distributed among them their livelihood﴾. They cannot deny this. They know that among them are rich and poor, strong and weak, intelligent and dull, wise and foolish. They know this.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, making people of different degrees, by His words: ﴿so that some of them may take others in service﴾.
* Among the benefits of the verse: establishing causation and wisdom in the acts of Allah, the Exalted. That is, He, the Mighty and Majestic, acts for a wisdom; it must be for a wisdom, by His words: ﴿so that some of them may take others in service﴾, because the "lam" here indicates causation. The causation of Allah's cosmic decrees is abundant in the Qur'an. Are the legal rulings, such as obligation, prohibition, and permissibility, causally explained?
The answer: yes, they are causally explained. Every ruling of Allah, cosmic or legislative, must have a wisdom. But here is a question: are these wisdoms known to creation, or are they not known?
The answer: some of them are known, and some of them are not known. Is that not so?
* Students: Yes indeed.
* Shaykh: Because our intellects are deficient. However much intellect we reach, it is deficient.
So take this benefit: all the cosmic and legislative rulings of Allah are causally explained by a wisdom. But some of the wisdoms we know, and some we do not know. This is how it must be.
If someone says: which is more eloquent in worship, that one worships Allah without knowing the wisdom, or that one worships Allah knowing the wisdom?
The answer: as for complete humility, a person's worship of something whose wisdom he does not know is more eloquent than his worship of something whose wisdom he knows, because if he worships Allah with something whose wisdom he knows, he may be worshipping Allah for the sake of that wisdom. But if he does not know the wisdom, it becomes more eloquent in humility, as if he is saying: "I will worship Allah whether I know the wisdom of this or not."
An example of this is throwing the pebbles at the Jamarat during Hajj. A person brings specific pebbles and throws them at a specific place. Whereas if he brought many times these pebbles after ten days and threw them at this place, it would be considered pointless. So what is the wisdom?

Answer: The wisdom behind that is to establish the remembrance of Allah; for this reason, whenever a person throws, he says, "Allahu akbar." Second: it manifests the effect of pure devotion (ta'abbud mutlaq), whereby a person performs this action without knowing its precise purpose, and similar matters are many.

For this reason, the jurists (fuqaha'), may Allah have mercy on them, applied the term ta'abbudiyyah (acts of pure devotion) to rulings whose wisdom is not known, or said "this is ta'abbud" or the like, because its purpose is nothing other than establishing worship of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the permissibility of employing workers, from His words: ﴿that some of them may take others in service⁠﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the great wisdom in this, namely in the disparity (among people), for were it not for this disparity, the value of Allah's blessing would not be recognized in the wealthy with wealth, in the intelligent with intellect, in the strong with strength, and so on. Is that not so?

* Students: Yes indeed.

* The Shaykh: Yes. Were it not for madness, the value of intellect would not be recognized; were it not for sickness, the value of health would not be recognized. Do you agree with this?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: So then, this is part of the wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which includes Paradise, is better than what they amass, that is, better than everything they gather; for Allah is the goal that every believer strives for, indeed every sensible person must strive for it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication of the danger of accumulation, that is, the accumulation of wealth, and that this may cause one to forget the Hereafter. And so it is: the accumulation of wealth causes one to forget the Hereafter, except for those whom my Lord has mercy upon. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear that the world will be opened up to you, and you will compete for it as those before you competed for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3158) and Muslim (2961/6) from the hadith of 'Amr ibn 'Awf al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording: "...So rejoice and hope for what pleases you, for by Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear that the world will be spread out for you as it was spread out for those before you, and you will compete for it as they competed for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them." The hadith.]] This is the reality: worldly life and religion generally do not coexist, except for those whom Allah has mercy upon. How many a person was poor yet upright upon the religion of Allah, then Allah made him rich, and his riches became the cause of his transgression and his independence from his Lord. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Nay! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient⁠﴾ [Al-'Alaq 6–7].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 43, verses 33–39 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community [of disbelief], We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33], and so on to the end. ﴿Law-la﴾ (if not / were it not) is a particle that contains a condition: "law-la such-and-such, then such-and-such would have occurred." It is a particle of prohibition due to the existence of something. ﴿Were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have given﴾: the bestowing was prevented lest mankind become one community. ﴿Were it not that mankind would be one community﴾ upon what? Upon disbelief. The evidence is His saying: ﴿We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33]. ﴿We would have given﴾ means: We would have made. ﴿Those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾ means Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. ﴿For their houses﴾ is a substitution (badal) from ﴿for those who﴾?

What kind of substitution is it? The substitution was covered recently.

* Student: Ishtimal (inclusive substitution).

* The Shaykh: It is an inclusive substitution (badal ishtimal): ﴿We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses﴾. The substitution is the intended object of the ruling, so the meaning is: We would have given to the houses of those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful.

﴿Suqufan﴾ (roofs) is read with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, meaning the singular ﴿saqfan﴾ (a roof). When read with a damma on both, it is the plural ﴿suqufan﴾.

The mufassir said: "with this and with this." Does that mean they are two readings?

The answer is yes: they are two canonical readings (qira'at sab'iyya, of the seven recognized readings), because neither was transmitted to the exclusion of the other. Both are sound. This is also part of his style, may Allah have mercy on him: when he says "with this and with this," they are two canonical readings.

So it is permissible for you to recite: ﴿for their houses, a roof of silver﴾, or ﴿for their houses, roofs of silver﴾. Do you understand?

﴿Of silver﴾ is known. (﴿And stairways﴾, like staircases, also of silver; ﴿upon which they ascend﴾: they climb to the roof.) ﴿And for their houses﴾ means: and We would have given their houses also ﴿doors﴾, meaning (of silver). And We would have given them ﴿couches﴾, meaning (of silver, the plural of sarir), ﴿upon which they recline﴾, meaning they lean. ﴿And adornment﴾: (gold).

Listen to this picture. The meaning is: were it not that the people would all disbelieve, We would have given these disbelievers houses with roofs of silver, instead of roofs of wood or cast cement. The intended silver is a shining silver that attracts the eye and pleases the sight.

﴿Stairways upon which they ascend﴾: it is said they are staircases. Some later scholars said they are electric elevators called "asansir" (elevators), lifts, and similar things, because ordinary staircases do not attract much attention. That is why He said ﴿upon which they ascend﴾, meaning they climb until they reach the roof. Whichever of these it is, they are unusual stairways, not ordinary ones. The third view is that they are doors.

* Students: Doors.

* The Shaykh: Doors. The author says "of silver," based on what was mentioned at the beginning of the verse, ﴿roofs of silver﴾. But this is not determined. Rather we say: ﴿doors﴾: magnificent doors, not like the usual ones, whether of silver, iron, or wood. The point is that they are unusual doors.

﴿And couches﴾, the plural of sarir, which is what one sits upon. ﴿Upon which they recline﴾: along with the couches there is also a cushion to lean on, meaning they rest upon it, whether behind the back, on the right, or on the left. This is a metaphor for great luxury.

﴿And adornment﴾ is this gold. So how many items is that? Roofs of silver, stairways upon which they ascend, magnificent doors, comfortable couches, adornment, meaning gold. Five things. The meaning is: (Were it not that disbelief would be a temptation for the believer through giving the disbeliever what was mentioned, We would have given him that, because the worldly life is of little worth to Us and he has no share of bliss in the Hereafter.)

The reason for this is that souls incline to amusement, play, and luxury. When a person sees this luxury given to a disbeliever, it entices and deceives him, as is done now by the missionaries, the misguided Christians, who go into poor regions and make the worldly life appear attractive, and these poor people follow them, because souls are naturally disposed to love wealth, pride, and vanity.

The Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And all that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ [az-Zukhruf 35]. The mufassir said: (in is a lightened form of the heavy particle), the heavy form whose doubling has been removed. (In is a lightened form of the heavy particle. ﴿All that la-ma﴾ is read with lightening, so ma is superfluous; with doubling it means "except"). That is, there are two readings: ﴿la-ma﴾ and ﴿lamma﴾. (So in is a negating particle.) The author confused the matter, may Allah have mercy on him.

Now he parsed in as a lightened form of the heavy particle, which is emphatic, then at the end he said in is negating. There is a difference between affirmation and negation. But this depends on la-ma: if it is read lightened, then in is the lightened form of the heavy particle, and if it is read doubled, then in is negating. Pay attention.

So the difference in grammatical analysis of in is based on the difference in the reading of la-ma. On the doubled reading, in is negating and la-ma means "except," and the evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Each soul has over it a guardian﴾ [at-Tariq 4], meaning: no soul except that it has over it a guardian. But if la-ma is read lightened, then in is the lightened form of the heavy particle, and ma is superfluous, and the construction is: "Indeed all that is the enjoyment of the worldly life," because ma is superfluous. Please pay attention.

La-ma has two readings. The first is doubling. On this reading, in is negating and lamma means "except," and the evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Each soul has over it a guardian﴾, meaning: no soul except that it has over it a guardian. The second reading is la-ma with lightening. On this reading, in is the lightened form of the heavy particle, meaning inna, and ma is superfluous, and the sentence means: Indeed all that is the enjoyment of the worldly life. Is that clear or not clear?

* The students: Clear.

* The Shaykh: The author, may Allah have mercy on him, combined the two readings, but this is the detailed explanation. What is the detail?

* Student: If lamma is doubled...

* The Shaykh: If lamma is doubled.

* Student: Then in is negating.

* The Shaykh: Then in is negating.

* Student: And lamma means "except."

* The Shaykh: And lamma means "except," correct. The construction is: "No soul except that it has over it..."

* Student: If it is lightened, then in is the lightened form of the heavy particle.

* The Shaykh: It is the lightened form of the heavy particle, so it is an emphatic particle, and ma...

* Student: And ma is superfluous.

* The Shaykh: And ma is superfluous, and the construction is: "Indeed all that is the enjoyment of the worldly life," because ma is superfluous.

﴿The enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ is what one enjoys in it and then it passes away. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾, which is Paradise, ﴿is with your Lord for the righteous﴾. Had it been said "the whole Hereafter: Paradise, the gatherings of Resurrection, their safety from the terror of the Day of Resurrection, and other things," it would have been more general. So the worldly life belongs to the disbelievers, however much they are given, and that is their bliss. The Hereafter belongs to the righteous, may Allah make us and you among them.

Know that this worldly life is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. However much bliss it reaches, it is a prison for the believer, and however much hellfire it reaches, it is a paradise for the disbeliever. Listen to the story. What did we say?

* Student: That the world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. However much bliss it reaches, it is a prison for the believer, and however much punishment it reaches, it is a paradise for the disbeliever.

* The Shaykh: This is a story that the scholars mentioned in the biography of Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him. Ibn Hajar was the Chief Judge in Egypt. One day he passed from his house to his workplace in a carriage pulled by horses or mules in a procession. One day he passed a Jewish man who was an oil seller (zayyat, meaning he sold oil). The Jew stopped the Chief Judge and said: "Your Prophet says: the world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. How does this agree with my condition and yours? You are now in bliss, drawn by horses, and you have status, honor, and rank. And I, the Jew, am in this humiliation, with dirty clothes and hardship. How is this?"

Do you know what he said?

He said: "Yes. What I am in now, compared to the bliss of Paradise, is a prison, because the bliss of Paradise is higher and higher than this. As for you, you are in a paradise compared to the punishment of the Fire, because if you die upon Judaism you will be in the Fire. And what the Jew is in now is considered a paradise. The Jew, as it appears to me, and Allah knows best, is seeking the truth, wanting the truth." When Ibn Hajar explained this to him, he said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Glory be to Allah! A sensible person who seeks the truth must be guided.

In any case, the Exalted and Majestic, after mentioning these things, said: ﴿For their houses, roofs of silver﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33], to the end, and said: this is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. Look, enjoyment is like the provisions a traveler carries. ﴿And the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous﴾ [az-Zukhruf 35], because however long a person's life in this world, it must end. Either the world will leave him, or he will leave the world. The poet said:

There is no pleasure in life while its delights are troubled
by remembering death and old age.

Indeed, when a person remembers, he realizes that his end is either an early death or a decrepit old age. Today there are people who have reached a very old age and reached the stage of senility. They themselves are distressed, and their families are distressed. You find a person annoyed with his father and mother. Even if the believer is patient, he must be distressed, or there must be a sudden death and the matter ends. This is the reality of the world. Therefore, seize the opportunity, seize the opportunity, hasten to do good before your life passes. Do righteous deeds, and seeking knowledge is among the best deeds, on condition that the scholar acts upon it. As for knowledge without action, by Allah, ignorance is better than it.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. The rule is: the lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the cause. The verse ﴿So that some of them may take others as subordinates﴾ [az-Zukhruf 32]. Why does it not carry both meanings: mockery, and also the other meaning?

* The Shaykh: And what is the other?

* Student: Mockery, and also...

* The Shaykh: No, that does not hold, because the difference in social classes is not so that some should mock others. Rather it is so that some should make others serve through work. It is impossible that Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, in His wisdom, would make classes differ so that they could mock one another.

* Student: The saying of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33], until He said: ﴿and adornment﴾ [az-Zukhruf 35]. Does His saying ﴿and adornment﴾ include what the silver included, meaning that He makes the houses...?

* The Shaykh: The point is that it is gold, whether it is a roof made of gold, or gold statues, or other things. It is general.

* Student: The author says: ﴿And your Lord's mercy﴾, meaning that it is Paradise. Is this part of his interpretation?

* The Shaykh: No, it is from the division within tafsir. There is no doubt that it is interpretation (ta'wil), because Paradise is mercy. We mentioned that Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, said to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will." But restricting it to certain types of mercy (...).

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. (36) And indeed they bar them from the way, while they think that they are guided. (37) Until, when he comes to Us, he says: "Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!" (38) And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾ [az-Zukhruf 36–39]

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. The Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾. After He mentioned the conditions of the world, and that were it not that mankind would become one community upon disbelief, He would have given the disbelievers what you have heard, and this world must lead a person to turn away from the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. He said: ﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil﴾.

His saying ﴿yaʿshu﴾ (turns blind): the mufassir explained it as (turns away). But the precise explanation is that the meaning of ﴿ya'shu﴾ is: he feigns blindness, until he sees like one who is night-blind, who sees in daylight but not at night. So the meaning of ﴿ya'shu﴾ is: he feigns blindness, as Ibn Kathir and other exegetes explained it. But the mufassir explained it as (turns away), because turning away is a necessary consequence of feigned blindness. He said: (﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the Qur'an). So the mufassir made "the remembrance of the Most Merciful" mean the Qur'an, and Allah attributed it to the Most Merciful because its sending down is mercy to creation. Thus the mufassir, may Allah have mercy on him, proceeded in this way.

The correct view is otherwise. The intended meaning of ﴿the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾ is remembering the Most Merciful, meaning: whoever feigns blindness to the remembrance of the Most Merciful in his heart, and fails to hold in mind the greatness and majesty of his Lord, a devil is assigned to him as a consequence of his turning away and blindness to the remembrance of his Lord. This is like His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will make him enter a severe punishment﴾ [al-Jinn 17]. So the correct view is that the intended meaning of ﴿the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾ is not the Qur'an, but the remembrance of Allah Himself. That is, his heart becomes heedless of the remembrance of Allah and does not remember Allah in his heart. This is the one for whom Satan is assigned, so he follows his desire, as the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair is excess﴾ [al-Kahf 28].

As for His saying ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾ [az-Zukhruf 36], the mufassir said: (We cause him to be accompanied by), which is close to the precise meaning. Otherwise, the meaning of ﴿nuqayyid﴾ is: We prepare for him a devil who takes the place of the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, so Satan takes control of his heart. Satan grows through indecency and wrongdoing, as Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿The Satan promises you poverty and commands you to indecency, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Himself and bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 268].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 43, verse 33–39 (part 2 of 2):

﴿We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his constant companion.﴾ Then he, that is the devil, ﴿for him﴾, that is for the one who turns away from the remembrance of Allah, is a companion who never leaves him. We seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. The reason for this is that a human being is active, willful, and in motion, both in heart and in body, so he must occupy himself with something. Either it will be the remembrance of Allah, or it will be the whispers of Shaytan, and there is no alternative. You will not find anyone whose heart is still, not moving and not willing; this is impossible. For this reason, a hadith about names has come: «The most beloved of names to Allah are ʿAbd al-Rahman (servant of the Most Merciful), and the most truthful of them are Harith (the one who works) and Hammam (the one who strives)». [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4950) from the hadith of Abu Wahb al-Jushami, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Hammam refers to the worship of the heart, and Harith refers to action. Every person necessarily has one of these, so this Shaytan is prepared for him, the one who accompanies him and never leaves him.
(﴿And indeed they﴾, that is the devils, ﴿surely bar them﴾, that is the ones who turn away, ﴿from the path﴾, that is the way of guidance, ﴿while they think they are rightly guided﴾.)
﴿while they think﴾, that is, those who turn away and whom the devils have diverted, ﴿that they are rightly guided﴾ (the plural here observes the meaning of "man").
When Shaytan, we seek refuge with Allah from him, takes control of a person's heart, he makes the evil of his deeds seem attractive to him, and he thinks he is upon the truth while he is upon falsehood. These are the people with the greatest loss in deeds, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ [al-Kahf 103]. The answer: yes, Allah has explained them. He said: ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good work﴾ [al-Kahf 104]; because Shaytan made this attractive to them, and said: You are upon the truth, you are the superior ones, and he beautified it for them and gave them false hope until they followed him.
For this reason he said: (﴿And indeed they﴾, meaning the devils, ﴿surely bar them﴾, that is the ones who turn away, ﴿from the path﴾) that is the path of truth and the way of guidance, ﴿while they think﴾. The waw refers to whom?
* Student: To (the ones who turn away).
* The Shaykh: It refers to (the ones who turn away). ﴿that they﴾, that is the ones who turn away, ﴿are rightly guided﴾, that is, upon guidance. This is the utmost of loss, and we seek refuge with Allah, that a person persists in falsehood while thinking that he is upon the truth.
The commentator said: (the plural here observes the meaning of "man"). The plural is His saying: ﴿they think﴾, ﴿indeed they surely bar them﴾. So in it there is observance of the meaning of "man" in His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away﴾. The word "man", "ma", and similar general expressions may be read according to their meaning or according to their wording. The wording is singular or plural? Singular. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾; therefore the pronoun returns to it in the singular, ﴿And whoever turns away﴾, ﴿We appoint for him﴾, also observing the wording, ﴿so he is his﴾, observing the wording, ﴿And indeed they surely bar them﴾, observing the meaning, ﴿and they think that they are rightly guided﴾, likewise observing the meaning. Is it clear?
So if "man", whether relative or conditional, comes to you, you may observe its wording in its pronoun and make it singular, or observe its meaning and make it according to what is intended. Consider His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Talaq 11]. All of this is observing what?
* Students: The wording.
* The Shaykh: The wording. ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, observing the meaning. ﴿Allah has provided excellently for him﴾, observing the wording. ﴿Allah has provided excellently for him a provision﴾ [al-Talaq 11]. So you find these verses sometimes observe the wording and sometimes observe the meaning. ﴿while they think that they are rightly guided﴾.
(﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, the one who turns away, with his companion on the Day of Resurrection, he says: ﴿O﴾, for alerting, ﴿would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts﴾, that is like the distance between the east and the west, ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾, you are to me).
﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, meaning the devil and his companion, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, each disowns the other, and he says to him: ﴿O would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts﴾. ﴿O﴾ here is for alerting, and it cannot be for calling, because the ﴿O﴾ used for calling enters only upon a noun, not upon a particle as here, nor upon a verb. So when you find it entering upon a particle or a verb, it is for alerting.
﴿O would that between me and you﴾, and similar to it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It was said: Enter Paradise. He said: Would that my people knew﴾ [Ya-Sin 26]. So it is for alerting. It has been said that ﴿O﴾ enters upon an omitted vocative, and the estimate in this verse is: O you, would that between me and you were after the two easts; that is, you estimate a noun as the vocative: O you, O would that between me and you.
If someone says: which is preferable, that we estimate a vocative that fits the context so that the placing of ﴿O﴾ in this position is valid, or we say: the basic principle is no estimation, and we make ﴿O﴾ for alerting?
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second is preferable, because when it is uncertain whether there is something omitted in the speech or not, it is preferable that there be nothing omitted.
As for His saying: ﴿the distance of the two easts﴾, the author says: (what is between the east and the west). Accordingly there is in the speech a taghlib (prevalence), namely the prevalence of the east over the west. This taghlib is permissible in the Arabic language, like the saying of the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family: «Between every two calls to prayer there is a prayer». [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (627) and Muslim (838/304) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, may Allah be pleased with him.]] If we take the general meaning of "adhan" as the call that occurs at every time, then this is so. But if we take adhan in the sense of announcement, then "the two adhans" contains no taghlib, because both the iqama and the adhan are called adhan.
But their saying "al-Qamarān" (the two moons), they mean by it the sun and the moon; their saying "al-ʿUmarān" (the two ʿUmars), they mean by it Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. This is from the category of taghlib. So ﴿the distance of the two easts﴾ means the distance between the east and the west, but it is mentioned with the word "east" by way of taghlib.
It may also mean ﴿the distance of the two easts﴾, that is the two risings of the sun, its rising in winter and its rising in summer, because between them is a very great distance whose extent none knows except Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Both meanings are correct, that is, whether we take the wording to contain taghlib or not. The meaning is that this person who was misled by Shaytan, when he comes with him on the Day of Resurrection, disowns him and says: Would that you were far from me, and I am far from you.
As for His saying: ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾, this sentence is an exclamatory expression of blame. The author said: "you", meaning that the specified subject has been omitted from it, because "bi'sa" and "ni'ma" necessarily require an agent and a specified subject. The details of this are in the books of grammar, and we need not discuss it here.
Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And it will not benefit you﴾, that is the ones who turn away, your wishing and your regret, ﴿today, since you have wronged﴾, that is, your wrongdoing through associating partners in the world has become clear to you, that you are, together with your companions, ﴿in the punishment, sharing﴾, a cause with the lam implied; because of the absence of benefit, and ﴿since﴾ is a substitute for ﴿today﴾). That is, your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you. This is the correct view, and on this basis ﴿that you﴾ is not for causation, as the commentator held, but is the subject of "yanfa'a" (benefit), and the meaning is that your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you. The reason for this is that it is customary that when a person is punished and sees others being punished, the matter becomes easier for him and he is consoled. On the Day of Resurrection the people of the Fire share in the punishment, but does this benefit them at all? It does not benefit them. This is the correct reading that the verse indicates. As for the author, he made ﴿that you﴾ ("anna") (a cause with the lam implied), meaning that you are sharing in the punishment, but this is far from the wording.
When Allah mentioned what He has prepared for the disbelievers, He said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would become one community﴾, and then He said: ﴿And all that...﴾ to the end.
* There are benefits in this verse: that these worldly enjoyments are nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world, and they are transient. Following from this benefit, a person should not attach himself to them, nor be preoccupied with them, and he should see that he lives without them. "You possess of this world only what you eat and it is consumed, or what you wear and it wears out, or what you give in charity and it passes on."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouraging indifference toward these matters and not being preoccupied with them. Do not attach your heart to the outward appearances of this world, for if you do, you will perish. For this reason, when the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family, saw something of the world that pleased him, he said: «Labbayk (here I am), indeed life is the life of the Hereafter». [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi (9035) from the hadith of Mujahid as a mursal report.]] "Labbayk" means in answer to you, so that he turns his heart away from attachment to what he saw that pleased him in the world. Then he settled himself and said: «Indeed life is the life of the Hereafter». By Allah, this is the truth: the life of this world, however pleasant it is for you, is surrounded by hardship before it and hardship after it, because you usually do not obtain it except with toil; then once you obtain it, will it remain for you or not? It must be that either you die and leave it, or it perishes while you are alive.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: glad tidings for the God-fearing, and that for them is the Hereafter. The Hereafter is better for the God-fearing. This contains good news that the God-fearing person, when he departs from this world, does not regret, because he has moved to an abode better and finer than what he left.
* And in it: encouragement toward taqwa (God-consciousness), because the mention of reward and recompense stirs the soul until a person reaches the quality by which he earns the reward.
Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion﴾, to the end.
* In this noble verse there are benefits:
* Among them: a warning against heedlessness of the remembrance of Allah, because when you are heedless of the remembrance of Allah, what takes the place of the remembrance of Allah is what? The whispers of Shaytan.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes the servant with what the sin requires. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut 40]. This man, when he emptied his heart of the remembrance of Allah, was punished by having Shaytan take its place.
* And among them: a warning against evil companions, because "Shayatin" is not a term specific to the devils of the jinn; even humans have shayatin, is that not so?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-Anʿam 112], and the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾ [al-Nas 1] to His saying: ﴿of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [al-Nas 6].
In this is a warning against evil companions, and the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family, warned against evil companions, comparing the evil companion or evil companion-sitter to the bellows-blower: either he burns your clothes, or you find from him a foul smell. Indeed the reality is so; how often do we receive calls from people who complain about a group who were upright, imams or muezzins of mosques, and then people of evil companionship contacted them and they deviated completely. Such people, we seek refuge with Allah, when they deviate, we ask Allah for steadfastness, their deviation is more severe and greater, like water you have held back and then released, it will rush out with force.
The point is that when a person turns away from the remembrance of Allah, Shaytan is appointed for him from mankind. Complete.
* Student: And from the jinn.
* The Shaykh: And from the jinn, so he has a companion.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the constant companion has a stronger effect than the worshipper who accompanies you and remains your companion. The constant companion has a stronger effect than the worshipper; meaning, if you sit with a person of evil character for an hour or two, it may affect you, and you may be affected, but if he is a constant companion, he will certainly influence you. For this reason He said: ﴿so he is his companion﴾.
I say this so that you beware of continuing with evil companions, and so that you know that once you know someone is an evil companion, it is obligatory to distance yourself from him. Do not say: I fear he will be affected, I fear he will say: why? The man was my friend and then left me? Do not mind that; what should concern you is yourself, so rescue it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: blindness of the heart, and we seek refuge with Allah. When a person is blind in his eye to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, his heart is also appointed a devil who bars him from guidance while he thinks he is guided: ﴿And indeed they surely bar them from the path, while they think that they are rightly guided﴾ [al-Zukhruf 37]. And this is very common: people of innovation who insisted on their innovations, small or great, did they not find them good?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Why did they find them good, when they are misguided innovation? Because Shaytan barred them from the truth. People of corrupt ideas, such as the secularists, communists, Ba'athists, and those like them, why did they persist in that? Because Shaytan has taken hold of their hearts, we seek refuge with Allah, and made them think that this evil is good. This is the gravest of trials: that a person sees evil as good and then proceeds in it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that some suspicion is sinful. Its reason is that these people thought they were upon the truth, so they persisted in falsehood.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that this companion in the world disowns his companion on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿O would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts; so wretched is the companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf 38].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that even with his wish, which gains him nothing, he praises his companion with blame and disparagement, saying: ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that among companions there is one who is a companion of good and a companion of evil, and so it is. The Prophet ﷺ made this clearest of all when he said: «The likeness of the good companion is like the bearer of musk: either he will give you a gift» (meaning he will give you a present), «or he will sell to you, or you will find from him a pleasant fragrance; and the companion of evil is like the bellows-blower: either he will burn your clothes with the sparks that fly from the fire when it is blown, or you will find from him a foul smell». [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534) and Muslim (2628/146) from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, and the wording is: "The likeness of the good companion and the evil one is like the bearer of musk and the bellows-blower. As for the bearer of musk: either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will find a pleasant fragrance from him. As for the bellows-blower: either he will burn your clothes, or you will find a foul odor."]]
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged﴾ [al-Zukhruf 39]: that those who share in the punishment of the Hereafter are not benefited by sharing it, unlike sharing in punishment in this world, which consoles a person and makes it easier for him. For this reason al-Khansa said in lamenting her brother Sakhr:
Were it not for the great number of weepers around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.
They do not weep like my brother, but I console myself about him with consolation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these tormented ones are the ones who wronged, and they were not wronged, as shown by His saying: ﴿since you have wronged﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that they, that is the tormented, know that they share in the punishment, but that does not console them or make the calamity easier for them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 43, verses 33–39 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community [of disbelief], We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33], and so on to the end. ﴿Law-la﴾ (if not / were it not) is a particle that contains a condition: "law-la such-and-such, then such-and-such would have occurred." It is a particle of prohibition due to the existence of something. ﴿Were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have given﴾: the bestowing was prevented lest mankind become one community. ﴿Were it not that mankind would be one community﴾ upon what? Upon disbelief. The evidence is His saying: ﴿We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33]. ﴿We would have given﴾ means: We would have made. ﴿Those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾ means Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. ﴿For their houses﴾ is a substitution (badal) from ﴿for those who﴾?

What kind of substitution is it? The substitution was covered recently.

* Student: Ishtimal (inclusive substitution).

* The Shaykh: It is an inclusive substitution (badal ishtimal): ﴿We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses﴾. The substitution is the intended object of the ruling, so the meaning is: We would have given to the houses of those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful.

﴿Suqufan﴾ (roofs) is read with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, meaning the singular ﴿saqfan﴾ (a roof). When read with a damma on both, it is the plural ﴿suqufan﴾.

The mufassir said: "with this and with this." Does that mean they are two readings?

The answer is yes: they are two canonical readings (qira'at sab'iyya, of the seven recognized readings), because neither was transmitted to the exclusion of the other. Both are sound. This is also part of his style, may Allah have mercy on him: when he says "with this and with this," they are two canonical readings.

So it is permissible for you to recite: ﴿for their houses, a roof of silver﴾, or ﴿for their houses, roofs of silver﴾. Do you understand?

﴿Of silver﴾ is known. (﴿And stairways﴾, like staircases, also of silver; ﴿upon which they ascend﴾: they climb to the roof.) ﴿And for their houses﴾ means: and We would have given their houses also ﴿doors﴾, meaning (of silver). And We would have given them ﴿couches﴾, meaning (of silver, the plural of sarir), ﴿upon which they recline﴾, meaning they lean. ﴿And adornment﴾: (gold).

Listen to this picture. The meaning is: were it not that the people would all disbelieve, We would have given these disbelievers houses with roofs of silver, instead of roofs of wood or cast cement. The intended silver is a shining silver that attracts the eye and pleases the sight.

﴿Stairways upon which they ascend﴾: it is said they are staircases. Some later scholars said they are electric elevators called "asansir" (elevators), lifts, and similar things, because ordinary staircases do not attract much attention. That is why He said ﴿upon which they ascend﴾, meaning they climb until they reach the roof. Whichever of these it is, they are unusual stairways, not ordinary ones. The third view is that they are doors.

* Students: Doors.

* The Shaykh: Doors. The author says "of silver," based on what was mentioned at the beginning of the verse, ﴿roofs of silver﴾. But this is not determined. Rather we say: ﴿doors﴾: magnificent doors, not like the usual ones, whether of silver, iron, or wood. The point is that they are unusual doors.

﴿And couches﴾, the plural of sarir, which is what one sits upon. ﴿Upon which they recline﴾: along with the couches there is also a cushion to lean on, meaning they rest upon it, whether behind the back, on the right, or on the left. This is a metaphor for great luxury.

﴿And adornment﴾ is this gold. So how many items is that? Roofs of silver, stairways upon which they ascend, magnificent doors, comfortable couches, adornment, meaning gold. Five things. The meaning is: (Were it not that disbelief would be a temptation for the believer through giving the disbeliever what was mentioned, We would have given him that, because the worldly life is of little worth to Us and he has no share of bliss in the Hereafter.)

The reason for this is that souls incline to amusement, play, and luxury. When a person sees this luxury given to a disbeliever, it entices and deceives him, as is done now by the missionaries, the misguided Christians, who go into poor regions and make the worldly life appear attractive, and these poor people follow them, because souls are naturally disposed to love wealth, pride, and vanity.

The Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And all that is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ [az-Zukhruf 35]. The mufassir said: (in is a lightened form of the heavy particle), the heavy form whose doubling has been removed. (In is a lightened form of the heavy particle. ﴿All that la-ma﴾ is read with lightening, so ma is superfluous; with doubling it means "except"). That is, there are two readings: ﴿la-ma﴾ and ﴿lamma﴾. (So in is a negating particle.) The author confused the matter, may Allah have mercy on him.

Now he parsed in as a lightened form of the heavy particle, which is emphatic, then at the end he said in is negating. There is a difference between affirmation and negation. But this depends on la-ma: if it is read lightened, then in is the lightened form of the heavy particle, and if it is read doubled, then in is negating. Pay attention.

So the difference in grammatical analysis of in is based on the difference in the reading of la-ma. On the doubled reading, in is negating and la-ma means "except," and the evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Each soul has over it a guardian﴾ [at-Tariq 4], meaning: no soul except that it has over it a guardian. But if la-ma is read lightened, then in is the lightened form of the heavy particle, and ma is superfluous, and the construction is: "Indeed all that is the enjoyment of the worldly life," because ma is superfluous. Please pay attention.

La-ma has two readings. The first is doubling. On this reading, in is negating and lamma means "except," and the evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Each soul has over it a guardian﴾, meaning: no soul except that it has over it a guardian. The second reading is la-ma with lightening. On this reading, in is the lightened form of the heavy particle, meaning inna, and ma is superfluous, and the sentence means: Indeed all that is the enjoyment of the worldly life. Is that clear or not clear?

* The students: Clear.

* The Shaykh: The author, may Allah have mercy on him, combined the two readings, but this is the detailed explanation. What is the detail?

* Student: If lamma is doubled...

* The Shaykh: If lamma is doubled.

* Student: Then in is negating.

* The Shaykh: Then in is negating.

* Student: And lamma means "except."

* The Shaykh: And lamma means "except," correct. The construction is: "No soul except that it has over it..."

* Student: If it is lightened, then in is the lightened form of the heavy particle.

* The Shaykh: It is the lightened form of the heavy particle, so it is an emphatic particle, and ma...

* Student: And ma is superfluous.

* The Shaykh: And ma is superfluous, and the construction is: "Indeed all that is the enjoyment of the worldly life," because ma is superfluous.

﴿The enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ is what one enjoys in it and then it passes away. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾, which is Paradise, ﴿is with your Lord for the righteous﴾. Had it been said "the whole Hereafter: Paradise, the gatherings of Resurrection, their safety from the terror of the Day of Resurrection, and other things," it would have been more general. So the worldly life belongs to the disbelievers, however much they are given, and that is their bliss. The Hereafter belongs to the righteous, may Allah make us and you among them.

Know that this worldly life is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. However much bliss it reaches, it is a prison for the believer, and however much hellfire it reaches, it is a paradise for the disbeliever. Listen to the story. What did we say?

* Student: That the world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. However much bliss it reaches, it is a prison for the believer, and however much punishment it reaches, it is a paradise for the disbeliever.

* The Shaykh: This is a story that the scholars mentioned in the biography of Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him. Ibn Hajar was the Chief Judge in Egypt. One day he passed from his house to his workplace in a carriage pulled by horses or mules in a procession. One day he passed a Jewish man who was an oil seller (zayyat, meaning he sold oil). The Jew stopped the Chief Judge and said: "Your Prophet says: the world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever. How does this agree with my condition and yours? You are now in bliss, drawn by horses, and you have status, honor, and rank. And I, the Jew, am in this humiliation, with dirty clothes and hardship. How is this?"

Do you know what he said?

He said: "Yes. What I am in now, compared to the bliss of Paradise, is a prison, because the bliss of Paradise is higher and higher than this. As for you, you are in a paradise compared to the punishment of the Fire, because if you die upon Judaism you will be in the Fire. And what the Jew is in now is considered a paradise. The Jew, as it appears to me, and Allah knows best, is seeking the truth, wanting the truth." When Ibn Hajar explained this to him, he said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Glory be to Allah! A sensible person who seeks the truth must be guided.

In any case, the Exalted and Majestic, after mentioning these things, said: ﴿For their houses, roofs of silver﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33], to the end, and said: this is nothing but the enjoyment of the worldly life. Look, enjoyment is like the provisions a traveler carries. ﴿And the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous﴾ [az-Zukhruf 35], because however long a person's life in this world, it must end. Either the world will leave him, or he will leave the world. The poet said:

There is no pleasure in life while its delights are troubled
by remembering death and old age.

Indeed, when a person remembers, he realizes that his end is either an early death or a decrepit old age. Today there are people who have reached a very old age and reached the stage of senility. They themselves are distressed, and their families are distressed. You find a person annoyed with his father and mother. Even if the believer is patient, he must be distressed, or there must be a sudden death and the matter ends. This is the reality of the world. Therefore, seize the opportunity, seize the opportunity, hasten to do good before your life passes. Do righteous deeds, and seeking knowledge is among the best deeds, on condition that the scholar acts upon it. As for knowledge without action, by Allah, ignorance is better than it.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. The rule is: the lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the cause. The verse ﴿So that some of them may take others as subordinates﴾ [az-Zukhruf 32]. Why does it not carry both meanings: mockery, and also the other meaning?

* The Shaykh: And what is the other?

* Student: Mockery, and also...

* The Shaykh: No, that does not hold, because the difference in social classes is not so that some should mock others. Rather it is so that some should make others serve through work. It is impossible that Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, in His wisdom, would make classes differ so that they could mock one another.

* Student: The saying of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33], until He said: ﴿and adornment﴾ [az-Zukhruf 35]. Does His saying ﴿and adornment﴾ include what the silver included, meaning that He makes the houses...?

* The Shaykh: The point is that it is gold, whether it is a roof made of gold, or gold statues, or other things. It is general.

* Student: The author says: ﴿And your Lord's mercy﴾, meaning that it is Paradise. Is this part of his interpretation?

* The Shaykh: No, it is from the division within tafsir. There is no doubt that it is interpretation (ta'wil), because Paradise is mercy. We mentioned that Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, said to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will." But restricting it to certain types of mercy (...).

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. (36) And indeed they bar them from the way, while they think that they are guided. (37) Until, when he comes to Us, he says: "Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!" (38) And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾ [az-Zukhruf 36–39]

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. The Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾. After He mentioned the conditions of the world, and that were it not that mankind would become one community upon disbelief, He would have given the disbelievers what you have heard, and this world must lead a person to turn away from the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. He said: ﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil﴾.

His saying ﴿yaʿshu﴾ (turns blind): the mufassir explained it as (turns away). But the precise explanation is that the meaning of ﴿ya'shu﴾ is: he feigns blindness, until he sees like one who is night-blind, who sees in daylight but not at night. So the meaning of ﴿ya'shu﴾ is: he feigns blindness, as Ibn Kathir and other exegetes explained it. But the mufassir explained it as (turns away), because turning away is a necessary consequence of feigned blindness. He said: (﴿And whoever turns blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the Qur'an). So the mufassir made "the remembrance of the Most Merciful" mean the Qur'an, and Allah attributed it to the Most Merciful because its sending down is mercy to creation. Thus the mufassir, may Allah have mercy on him, proceeded in this way.

The correct view is otherwise. The intended meaning of ﴿the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾ is remembering the Most Merciful, meaning: whoever feigns blindness to the remembrance of the Most Merciful in his heart, and fails to hold in mind the greatness and majesty of his Lord, a devil is assigned to him as a consequence of his turning away and blindness to the remembrance of his Lord. This is like His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will make him enter a severe punishment﴾ [al-Jinn 17]. So the correct view is that the intended meaning of ﴿the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾ is not the Qur'an, but the remembrance of Allah Himself. That is, his heart becomes heedless of the remembrance of Allah and does not remember Allah in his heart. This is the one for whom Satan is assigned, so he follows his desire, as the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair is excess﴾ [al-Kahf 28].

As for His saying ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾ [az-Zukhruf 36], the mufassir said: (We cause him to be accompanied by), which is close to the precise meaning. Otherwise, the meaning of ﴿nuqayyid﴾ is: We prepare for him a devil who takes the place of the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, so Satan takes control of his heart. Satan grows through indecency and wrongdoing, as Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿The Satan promises you poverty and commands you to indecency, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Himself and bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah 268].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 43, verse 33–39 (part 2 of 2):

﴿We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his constant companion.﴾ Then he, that is the devil, ﴿for him﴾, that is for the one who turns away from the remembrance of Allah, is a companion who never leaves him. We seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. The reason for this is that a human being is active, willful, and in motion, both in heart and in body, so he must occupy himself with something. Either it will be the remembrance of Allah, or it will be the whispers of Shaytan, and there is no alternative. You will not find anyone whose heart is still, not moving and not willing; this is impossible. For this reason, a hadith about names has come: «The most beloved of names to Allah are ʿAbd al-Rahman (servant of the Most Merciful), and the most truthful of them are Harith (the one who works) and Hammam (the one who strives)». [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4950) from the hadith of Abu Wahb al-Jushami, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Hammam refers to the worship of the heart, and Harith refers to action. Every person necessarily has one of these, so this Shaytan is prepared for him, the one who accompanies him and never leaves him.
(﴿And indeed they﴾, that is the devils, ﴿surely bar them﴾, that is the ones who turn away, ﴿from the path﴾, that is the way of guidance, ﴿while they think they are rightly guided﴾.)
﴿while they think﴾, that is, those who turn away and whom the devils have diverted, ﴿that they are rightly guided﴾ (the plural here observes the meaning of "man").
When Shaytan, we seek refuge with Allah from him, takes control of a person's heart, he makes the evil of his deeds seem attractive to him, and he thinks he is upon the truth while he is upon falsehood. These are the people with the greatest loss in deeds, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ [al-Kahf 103]. The answer: yes, Allah has explained them. He said: ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good work﴾ [al-Kahf 104]; because Shaytan made this attractive to them, and said: You are upon the truth, you are the superior ones, and he beautified it for them and gave them false hope until they followed him.
For this reason he said: (﴿And indeed they﴾, meaning the devils, ﴿surely bar them﴾, that is the ones who turn away, ﴿from the path﴾) that is the path of truth and the way of guidance, ﴿while they think﴾. The waw refers to whom?
* Student: To (the ones who turn away).
* The Shaykh: It refers to (the ones who turn away). ﴿that they﴾, that is the ones who turn away, ﴿are rightly guided﴾, that is, upon guidance. This is the utmost of loss, and we seek refuge with Allah, that a person persists in falsehood while thinking that he is upon the truth.
The commentator said: (the plural here observes the meaning of "man"). The plural is His saying: ﴿they think﴾, ﴿indeed they surely bar them﴾. So in it there is observance of the meaning of "man" in His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away﴾. The word "man", "ma", and similar general expressions may be read according to their meaning or according to their wording. The wording is singular or plural? Singular. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾; therefore the pronoun returns to it in the singular, ﴿And whoever turns away﴾, ﴿We appoint for him﴾, also observing the wording, ﴿so he is his﴾, observing the wording, ﴿And indeed they surely bar them﴾, observing the meaning, ﴿and they think that they are rightly guided﴾, likewise observing the meaning. Is it clear?
So if "man", whether relative or conditional, comes to you, you may observe its wording in its pronoun and make it singular, or observe its meaning and make it according to what is intended. Consider His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Talaq 11]. All of this is observing what?
* Students: The wording.
* The Shaykh: The wording. ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, observing the meaning. ﴿Allah has provided excellently for him﴾, observing the wording. ﴿Allah has provided excellently for him a provision﴾ [al-Talaq 11]. So you find these verses sometimes observe the wording and sometimes observe the meaning. ﴿while they think that they are rightly guided﴾.
(﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, the one who turns away, with his companion on the Day of Resurrection, he says: ﴿O﴾, for alerting, ﴿would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts﴾, that is like the distance between the east and the west, ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾, you are to me).
﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾, meaning the devil and his companion, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, each disowns the other, and he says to him: ﴿O would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts﴾. ﴿O﴾ here is for alerting, and it cannot be for calling, because the ﴿O﴾ used for calling enters only upon a noun, not upon a particle as here, nor upon a verb. So when you find it entering upon a particle or a verb, it is for alerting.
﴿O would that between me and you﴾, and similar to it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It was said: Enter Paradise. He said: Would that my people knew﴾ [Ya-Sin 26]. So it is for alerting. It has been said that ﴿O﴾ enters upon an omitted vocative, and the estimate in this verse is: O you, would that between me and you were after the two easts; that is, you estimate a noun as the vocative: O you, O would that between me and you.
If someone says: which is preferable, that we estimate a vocative that fits the context so that the placing of ﴿O﴾ in this position is valid, or we say: the basic principle is no estimation, and we make ﴿O﴾ for alerting?
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second is preferable, because when it is uncertain whether there is something omitted in the speech or not, it is preferable that there be nothing omitted.
As for His saying: ﴿the distance of the two easts﴾, the author says: (what is between the east and the west). Accordingly there is in the speech a taghlib (prevalence), namely the prevalence of the east over the west. This taghlib is permissible in the Arabic language, like the saying of the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family: «Between every two calls to prayer there is a prayer». [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (627) and Muslim (838/304) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, may Allah be pleased with him.]] If we take the general meaning of "adhan" as the call that occurs at every time, then this is so. But if we take adhan in the sense of announcement, then "the two adhans" contains no taghlib, because both the iqama and the adhan are called adhan.
But their saying "al-Qamarān" (the two moons), they mean by it the sun and the moon; their saying "al-ʿUmarān" (the two ʿUmars), they mean by it Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. This is from the category of taghlib. So ﴿the distance of the two easts﴾ means the distance between the east and the west, but it is mentioned with the word "east" by way of taghlib.
It may also mean ﴿the distance of the two easts﴾, that is the two risings of the sun, its rising in winter and its rising in summer, because between them is a very great distance whose extent none knows except Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Both meanings are correct, that is, whether we take the wording to contain taghlib or not. The meaning is that this person who was misled by Shaytan, when he comes with him on the Day of Resurrection, disowns him and says: Would that you were far from me, and I am far from you.
As for His saying: ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾, this sentence is an exclamatory expression of blame. The author said: "you", meaning that the specified subject has been omitted from it, because "bi'sa" and "ni'ma" necessarily require an agent and a specified subject. The details of this are in the books of grammar, and we need not discuss it here.
Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And it will not benefit you﴾, that is the ones who turn away, your wishing and your regret, ﴿today, since you have wronged﴾, that is, your wrongdoing through associating partners in the world has become clear to you, that you are, together with your companions, ﴿in the punishment, sharing﴾, a cause with the lam implied; because of the absence of benefit, and ﴿since﴾ is a substitute for ﴿today﴾). That is, your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you. This is the correct view, and on this basis ﴿that you﴾ is not for causation, as the commentator held, but is the subject of "yanfa'a" (benefit), and the meaning is that your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you. The reason for this is that it is customary that when a person is punished and sees others being punished, the matter becomes easier for him and he is consoled. On the Day of Resurrection the people of the Fire share in the punishment, but does this benefit them at all? It does not benefit them. This is the correct reading that the verse indicates. As for the author, he made ﴿that you﴾ ("anna") (a cause with the lam implied), meaning that you are sharing in the punishment, but this is far from the wording.
When Allah mentioned what He has prepared for the disbelievers, He said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would become one community﴾, and then He said: ﴿And all that...﴾ to the end.
* There are benefits in this verse: that these worldly enjoyments are nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world, and they are transient. Following from this benefit, a person should not attach himself to them, nor be preoccupied with them, and he should see that he lives without them. "You possess of this world only what you eat and it is consumed, or what you wear and it wears out, or what you give in charity and it passes on."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouraging indifference toward these matters and not being preoccupied with them. Do not attach your heart to the outward appearances of this world, for if you do, you will perish. For this reason, when the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family, saw something of the world that pleased him, he said: «Labbayk (here I am), indeed life is the life of the Hereafter». [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi (9035) from the hadith of Mujahid as a mursal report.]] "Labbayk" means in answer to you, so that he turns his heart away from attachment to what he saw that pleased him in the world. Then he settled himself and said: «Indeed life is the life of the Hereafter». By Allah, this is the truth: the life of this world, however pleasant it is for you, is surrounded by hardship before it and hardship after it, because you usually do not obtain it except with toil; then once you obtain it, will it remain for you or not? It must be that either you die and leave it, or it perishes while you are alive.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: glad tidings for the God-fearing, and that for them is the Hereafter. The Hereafter is better for the God-fearing. This contains good news that the God-fearing person, when he departs from this world, does not regret, because he has moved to an abode better and finer than what he left.
* And in it: encouragement toward taqwa (God-consciousness), because the mention of reward and recompense stirs the soul until a person reaches the quality by which he earns the reward.
Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion﴾, to the end.
* In this noble verse there are benefits:
* Among them: a warning against heedlessness of the remembrance of Allah, because when you are heedless of the remembrance of Allah, what takes the place of the remembrance of Allah is what? The whispers of Shaytan.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes the servant with what the sin requires. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut 40]. This man, when he emptied his heart of the remembrance of Allah, was punished by having Shaytan take its place.
* And among them: a warning against evil companions, because "Shayatin" is not a term specific to the devils of the jinn; even humans have shayatin, is that not so?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-Anʿam 112], and the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾ [al-Nas 1] to His saying: ﴿of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [al-Nas 6].
In this is a warning against evil companions, and the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family, warned against evil companions, comparing the evil companion or evil companion-sitter to the bellows-blower: either he burns your clothes, or you find from him a foul smell. Indeed the reality is so; how often do we receive calls from people who complain about a group who were upright, imams or muezzins of mosques, and then people of evil companionship contacted them and they deviated completely. Such people, we seek refuge with Allah, when they deviate, we ask Allah for steadfastness, their deviation is more severe and greater, like water you have held back and then released, it will rush out with force.
The point is that when a person turns away from the remembrance of Allah, Shaytan is appointed for him from mankind. Complete.
* Student: And from the jinn.
* The Shaykh: And from the jinn, so he has a companion.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the constant companion has a stronger effect than the worshipper who accompanies you and remains your companion. The constant companion has a stronger effect than the worshipper; meaning, if you sit with a person of evil character for an hour or two, it may affect you, and you may be affected, but if he is a constant companion, he will certainly influence you. For this reason He said: ﴿so he is his companion﴾.
I say this so that you beware of continuing with evil companions, and so that you know that once you know someone is an evil companion, it is obligatory to distance yourself from him. Do not say: I fear he will be affected, I fear he will say: why? The man was my friend and then left me? Do not mind that; what should concern you is yourself, so rescue it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: blindness of the heart, and we seek refuge with Allah. When a person is blind in his eye to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, his heart is also appointed a devil who bars him from guidance while he thinks he is guided: ﴿And indeed they surely bar them from the path, while they think that they are rightly guided﴾ [al-Zukhruf 37]. And this is very common: people of innovation who insisted on their innovations, small or great, did they not find them good?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Why did they find them good, when they are misguided innovation? Because Shaytan barred them from the truth. People of corrupt ideas, such as the secularists, communists, Ba'athists, and those like them, why did they persist in that? Because Shaytan has taken hold of their hearts, we seek refuge with Allah, and made them think that this evil is good. This is the gravest of trials: that a person sees evil as good and then proceeds in it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that some suspicion is sinful. Its reason is that these people thought they were upon the truth, so they persisted in falsehood.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that this companion in the world disowns his companion on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿O would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts; so wretched is the companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf 38].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that even with his wish, which gains him nothing, he praises his companion with blame and disparagement, saying: ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that among companions there is one who is a companion of good and a companion of evil, and so it is. The Prophet ﷺ made this clearest of all when he said: «The likeness of the good companion is like the bearer of musk: either he will give you a gift» (meaning he will give you a present), «or he will sell to you, or you will find from him a pleasant fragrance; and the companion of evil is like the bellows-blower: either he will burn your clothes with the sparks that fly from the fire when it is blown, or you will find from him a foul smell». [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534) and Muslim (2628/146) from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, and the wording is: "The likeness of the good companion and the evil one is like the bearer of musk and the bellows-blower. As for the bearer of musk: either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will find a pleasant fragrance from him. As for the bellows-blower: either he will burn your clothes, or you will find a foul odor."]]
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged﴾ [al-Zukhruf 39]: that those who share in the punishment of the Hereafter are not benefited by sharing it, unlike sharing in punishment in this world, which consoles a person and makes it easier for him. For this reason al-Khansa said in lamenting her brother Sakhr:
Were it not for the great number of weepers around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.
They do not weep like my brother, but I console myself about him with consolation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these tormented ones are the ones who wronged, and they were not wronged, as shown by His saying: ﴿since you have wronged﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that they, that is the tormented, know that they share in the punishment, but that does not console them or make the calamity easier for them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 43, verses 33–39 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community [of disbelief], We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33], and so on to the end. ﴿Law-la﴾ (if not / were it not) is a particle that contains a condition: "law-la such-and-such, then such-and-such would have occurred." It is a particle of prohibition due to the existence of something. ﴿Were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have given﴾: the bestowing was prevented lest mankind become one community. ﴿Were it not that mankind would be one community﴾ upon what? Upon disbelief. The evidence is His saying: ﴿We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses﴾ [az-Zukhruf 33]. ﴿We would have given﴾ means: We would have made. ﴿Those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾ means Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. ﴿For their houses﴾ is a substitution (badal) from ﴿for those who﴾?

What kind of substitution is it? The substitution was covered recently.

* Student: Ishtimal (inclusive substitution).

* The Shaykh: It is an inclusive substitution (badal ishtimal): ﴿We would have given to those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses﴾.
