As for His saying: ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾, this sentence is an exclamatory expression of blame. The author said: "you", meaning that the specified subject has been omitted from it, because "bi'sa" and "ni'ma" necessarily require an agent and a specified subject. The details of this are in the books of grammar, and we need not discuss it here.
Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And it will not benefit you﴾, that is the ones who turn away, your wishing and your regret, ﴿today, since you have wronged﴾, that is, your wrongdoing through associating partners in the world has become clear to you, that you are, together with your companions, ﴿in the punishment, sharing﴾, a cause with the lam implied; because of the absence of benefit, and ﴿since﴾ is a substitute for ﴿today﴾). That is, your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you. This is the correct view, and on this basis ﴿that you﴾ is not for causation, as the commentator held, but is the subject of "yanfa'a" (benefit), and the meaning is that your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you. The reason for this is that it is customary that when a person is punished and sees others being punished, the matter becomes easier for him and he is consoled. On the Day of Resurrection the people of the Fire share in the punishment, but does this benefit them at all? It does not benefit them. This is the correct reading that the verse indicates. As for the author, he made ﴿that you﴾ ("anna") (a cause with the lam implied), meaning that you are sharing in the punishment, but this is far from the wording.
When Allah mentioned what He has prepared for the disbelievers, He said: ﴿And were it not that mankind would become one community﴾, and then He said: ﴿And all that...﴾ to the end.
* There are benefits in this verse: that these worldly enjoyments are nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world, and they are transient. Following from this benefit, a person should not attach himself to them, nor be preoccupied with them, and he should see that he lives without them. "You possess of this world only what you eat and it is consumed, or what you wear and it wears out, or what you give in charity and it passes on."
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouraging indifference toward these matters and not being preoccupied with them. Do not attach your heart to the outward appearances of this world, for if you do, you will perish. For this reason, when the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family, saw something of the world that pleased him, he said: «Labbayk (here I am), indeed life is the life of the Hereafter». [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi (9035) from the hadith of Mujahid as a mursal report.]] "Labbayk" means in answer to you, so that he turns his heart away from attachment to what he saw that pleased him in the world. Then he settled himself and said: «Indeed life is the life of the Hereafter». By Allah, this is the truth: the life of this world, however pleasant it is for you, is surrounded by hardship before it and hardship after it, because you usually do not obtain it except with toil; then once you obtain it, will it remain for you or not? It must be that either you die and leave it, or it perishes while you are alive.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: glad tidings for the God-fearing, and that for them is the Hereafter. The Hereafter is better for the God-fearing. This contains good news that the God-fearing person, when he departs from this world, does not regret, because he has moved to an abode better and finer than what he left.
* And in it: encouragement toward taqwa (God-consciousness), because the mention of reward and recompense stirs the soul until a person reaches the quality by which he earns the reward.
Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he becomes his companion﴾, to the end.
* In this noble verse there are benefits:
* Among them: a warning against heedlessness of the remembrance of Allah, because when you are heedless of the remembrance of Allah, what takes the place of the remembrance of Allah is what? The whispers of Shaytan.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes the servant with what the sin requires. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut 40]. This man, when he emptied his heart of the remembrance of Allah, was punished by having Shaytan take its place.
* And among them: a warning against evil companions, because "Shayatin" is not a term specific to the devils of the jinn; even humans have shayatin, is that not so?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-Anʿam 112], and the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾ [al-Nas 1] to His saying: ﴿of the jinn and of mankind﴾ [al-Nas 6].
In this is a warning against evil companions, and the Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family, warned against evil companions, comparing the evil companion or evil companion-sitter to the bellows-blower: either he burns your clothes, or you find from him a foul smell. Indeed the reality is so; how often do we receive calls from people who complain about a group who were upright, imams or muezzins of mosques, and then people of evil companionship contacted them and they deviated completely. Such people, we seek refuge with Allah, when they deviate, we ask Allah for steadfastness, their deviation is more severe and greater, like water you have held back and then released, it will rush out with force.
The point is that when a person turns away from the remembrance of Allah, Shaytan is appointed for him from mankind. Complete.
* Student: And from the jinn.
* The Shaykh: And from the jinn, so he has a companion.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the constant companion has a stronger effect than the worshipper who accompanies you and remains your companion. The constant companion has a stronger effect than the worshipper; meaning, if you sit with a person of evil character for an hour or two, it may affect you, and you may be affected, but if he is a constant companion, he will certainly influence you. For this reason He said: ﴿so he is his companion﴾.
I say this so that you beware of continuing with evil companions, and so that you know that once you know someone is an evil companion, it is obligatory to distance yourself from him. Do not say: I fear he will be affected, I fear he will say: why? The man was my friend and then left me? Do not mind that; what should concern you is yourself, so rescue it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: blindness of the heart, and we seek refuge with Allah. When a person is blind in his eye to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, his heart is also appointed a devil who bars him from guidance while he thinks he is guided: ﴿And indeed they surely bar them from the path, while they think that they are rightly guided﴾ [al-Zukhruf 37]. And this is very common: people of innovation who insisted on their innovations, small or great, did they not find them good?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Why did they find them good, when they are misguided innovation? Because Shaytan barred them from the truth. People of corrupt ideas, such as the secularists, communists, Ba'athists, and those like them, why did they persist in that? Because Shaytan has taken hold of their hearts, we seek refuge with Allah, and made them think that this evil is good. This is the gravest of trials: that a person sees evil as good and then proceeds in it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that some suspicion is sinful. Its reason is that these people thought they were upon the truth, so they persisted in falsehood.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that this companion in the world disowns his companion on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿O would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts; so wretched is the companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf 38].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that even with his wish, which gains him nothing, he praises his companion with blame and disparagement, saying: ﴿So wretched is the companion﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that among companions there is one who is a companion of good and a companion of evil, and so it is. The Prophet ﷺ made this clearest of all when he said: «The likeness of the good companion is like the bearer of musk: either he will give you a gift» (meaning he will give you a present), «or he will sell to you, or you will find from him a pleasant fragrance; and the companion of evil is like the bellows-blower: either he will burn your clothes with the sparks that fly from the fire when it is blown, or you will find from him a foul smell». [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534) and Muslim (2628/146) from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, and the wording is: "The likeness of the good companion and the evil one is like the bearer of musk and the bellows-blower. As for the bearer of musk: either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will find a pleasant fragrance from him. As for the bellows-blower: either he will burn your clothes, or you will find a foul odor."]]
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged﴾ [al-Zukhruf 39]: that those who share in the punishment of the Hereafter are not benefited by sharing it, unlike sharing in punishment in this world, which consoles a person and makes it easier for him. For this reason al-Khansa said in lamenting her brother Sakhr:
Were it not for the great number of weepers around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.
They do not weep like my brother, but I console myself about him with consolation.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these tormented ones are the ones who wronged, and they were not wronged, as shown by His saying: ﴿since you have wronged﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that they, that is the tormented, know that they share in the punishment, but that does not console them or make the calamity easier for them.

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, then said: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind and those who are in manifest error?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 40]. Meaning: they do not believe. The hamzah (الهمزة, the interrogative particle) here carries the sense of negation, meaning that you cannot make the deaf hear or guide the blind, because this is entrusted to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And those who are in manifest error﴾: ḍalāl means error, and mubīn means clear. The hearing meant here is hearing the guidance, and the guiding meant here is guiding to the guidance. The meaning is not that you make the deaf hear your voice, for that is something everyone shares. But when the address is to the Messenger (ﷺ), the hearing means making the truth heard, and the guiding means guiding to the truth.

In this noble verse there is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ), for he would grieve over people's failure to be guided. Allah made clear to him that the matter is not in his hands but in Allah's. Then the calamity becomes easier for him, and he is content and submits, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the disbelievers are in the position of the deaf who do not hear. Allah described them in another verse as ﴿deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not understand﴾ [al-Baqarah 171], or ﴿deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not return﴾ [al-Baqarah 18].

Among its benefits: blindness is a cause of a person losing his way, from His saying ﴿or guide the blind﴾.

Among its benefits: whoever is in manifest error, meaning immersed in error, generally will not be guided.

Student: (...) Regarding ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْشُ﴾, does this refer to neglecting acts of obedience or committing prohibitions?

The Shaykh: The verse indicates a matter of the heart. ﴿مَنْ يَعْشُ﴾ means one who feigns blindness (يتعامى).

Student: So it has no connection to the limbs?

The Shaykh: No. When the heart is sound, the limbs are sound.

Student: The word المشارق (al-mashāriq) sometimes comes in the Qur'an in the singular, sometimes in the plural, and sometimes in the dual.

The Shaykh: المشارق, المشرق and المشرقين: yes, it comes in these three forms, and there is no contradiction between them. His saying ﴿Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but Him﴾ [al-Muzzammil 9] is singular, and al-mashriq here means the direction, since the directions are four: east, west, south and north. So al-mashriq means the direction of the east, and al-maghrib means the direction of the west.

As for "Lord of the easts and the wests" in the plural: it means the risings of the stars, the planets, the sun and the moon, since each of these has a rising. Or it means the risings of the sun, since the sun has a rising every day. Had it not been so, you would not see it moving from north to south and from south to north.

As for "Lord of the two easts and the two wests" in the dual: it means the two risings, of summer and of winter.

Student: May Allah reward you, O Shaykh. Regarding bad companions: if there is a deviant person, a man thinks that if he is with him, perhaps...

The Shaykh: He calls him, yes.

Student: Does it mean...?

The Shaykh: Does he keep his company? Or befriend him?

Student: Yes.

The Shaykh: That is not correct. Rather, he sits with him to call him to the truth and then leaves him, after calling him. For if he sticks to him, he is bound to be affected, and he does not know whether the upright will influence the deviant or the deviant will influence the upright. What is observed now is that, in most cases, the deviant influences the upright; this is what we know. So you do not keep his company. You come, for example, to visit him or invite him to your home, and you call him, but only that. As for accompanying him and making him a close companion, this is a great danger. A person's soul makes him think that if he keeps company with him he will be the cause of his reform, when the matter is the reverse. Take the example of a woman whom a deviant man proposes to, and she wishes to marry him, and says to herself, or her guardian says: "May Allah guide him; perhaps he will be guided if he marries." The matter ends up reversed: this upright woman becomes deviant through the whisperings of this husband.

Student: What is the duty of a person whose upright brother has deviated?

The Shaykh: From what aspect (...)?

Student: By advising him, or by cutting him off completely if he deviates, as you mentioned (...) from sins and from the world.

The Shaykh: Why would he not call him? Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not call his closest kinsmen? (...) Why does he not call him?

Student: He calls him, but he closes the door on him.

The Shaykh: How does he close the door? Does he imprison him?!

Student: No, if he comes to him to call him, he shuts the door against him and avoids him.

The Shaykh: The same (...). That's it, it does not matter. He seizes one opportunity or another and calls him.

* * *

Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan.

﴿So whether We take you away, We will surely take retribution from them. Or We show you what We have promised them, for We are fully capable over them. So hold fast to what has been revealed to you; indeed you are on a straight path. And indeed it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned. And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 41–45].

The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [al-Zukhruf 39]. What is the meaning of this verse?

Student: It means that when they are cast into the Fire, even if they are a group, this gathering will not benefit them, and they will not console themselves with it. In this world, gathering in evil does benefit them, and so on (...) in the punishment.

The Shaykh: It means that their sharing in punishment in the Hereafter will not benefit them, so that they console themselves with it as they do in this world.

His saying: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 40]. Brother, the interrogative: why? ﴿Can you make the deaf hear, or guide the blind?﴾ What is the meaning?

Student: It means you do not guide the blind.

The Shaykh: What?

Student: That you do not guide the blind.

The Shaykh: Where is the guidance? There is no guidance in the verse.

Student: You do not make the deaf hear (...).

The Shaykh: What?

Student: You speak, sir, and among men you said it is for negation. What is the meaning if it is for negation?

Student: The meaning is that you cannot make hear, from hearing the truth, the one who is deaf, and he does not see the guidance.

The Shaykh: Yes, good. What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And those who are in manifest error﴾?

Student: May Allah be good to you. (ḍalāl) is the opposite of guidance, and al-mubīn is the clear, the evident.

The Shaykh: And the meaning?

Student: The meaning is that you do not guide them.

The Shaykh: You do not guide those who are in manifest error. To whom does guidance belong? Who is it that guides?

Student: The one who guides, if it is the guidance of tawfīq (divine enabling), then it is...

The Shaykh: And if it is now, then it is the guidance of tawfīq. The Messenger presents to them the religion of truth.

Student: Then it belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Shaykh: That is, that belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So whether We take you away, indeed We will take vengeance upon them﴾ [az-Zukhruf 41].

﴿Fa-immā﴾: The commentator says: "In it there is idgham of the nun of (in)." That is, the conditional nun of (in) is assimilated into the extra (ma), so it becomes (immā). The original is (fa-in ma), but the sakin nun and the mim came together, so one was assimilated into the other, and it became ﴿immā nadhhabanna﴾.

As for his words "in the extra (ma)": know that there is nothing superfluous in the Qur'an. Everything in the Qur'an is in its proper place, and the context requires it. Revelation (wahy) is Allah's informing His messengers of what He prescribes for His servants.

﴿Indeed you are upon a straight path﴾ is an affirmation and a reassurance. The command is ﴿hold fast to that which has been revealed to you﴾; the reassurance is ﴿indeed you are upon a straight path﴾. And if one is upon a straight path, reason requires that he not deviate from it, but rather that he hold fast to it completely.

The sirat (path) is the wide, straight road. A narrow path is not called a sirat, and a crooked path turning right and left is not called a sirat; only what is a wide and straight road is called a sirat, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatiha 6], meaning the wide, straight road.

(﴿And indeed it is a reminder﴾ — an honour — ﴿for you and for your people﴾, because it was revealed in their language, ﴿and you will be questioned﴾ [az-Zukhruf 44] about discharging its rights). The "it" (wa innahu) refers to the Qur'an that was revealed to the Messenger ﷺ.

﴿Indeed it is a reminder for you﴾: "(an honour)" according to how the commentator explained it; that is, you are honoured by it, because it was revealed in your language and because it was revealed to one of you. So it is an honour. This is what the author (al-Mu'allif) adopted, and there is no objection to it. However, the correct view is that the meaning of "dhikr" here is "reminder": that this which has been revealed to you is a reminder for you and your people.

If someone says: this would apply to it being a reminder for all people.

The answer is that this is like His saying: ﴿He it is who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 2], although he was sent to all people. As for His saying ﴿and you will be questioned﴾: you will be questioned about what?

He says: "(about discharging its rights)", and among its rights is acting upon it and conveying it to people. For this reason, the Arabs are regarded as the radiant source for the general public in transmitting the Islamic Shari'ah.

Who was in the Arabian Peninsula when the revelation descended? There were none there but Arabs, and these Arabs spread Islam throughout all the regions of the world, and this is part of its rights.

﴿You will be questioned﴾ about what it contains of the command to jihad: did you strive or not? ﴿You will be questioned﴾ about implementing all its laws. For this reason, the author's statement here is good: "(about discharging its rights)".

He, the Exalted, said: (﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾, i.e., other than Him ﴿gods to be worshipped﴾ [az-Zukhruf 45]).

﴿Ask﴾ is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ, as shown by His saying ﴿those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾.

﴿Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ The answer would be: "No." The purpose of this command is to establish proof against the polytheists who worship another god alongside Allah. He tells the Prophet ﷺ: ask all the earlier messengers whether We appointed gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped, so that these polytheists may stand up and worship something else besides Allah. In this there is establishment of proof against the polytheists: that none of the earlier messengers permitted associating partners with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

If someone says: how can one ask those messengers whom Allah sent before him, when he did not meet them?

The answer is that this is one of the styles of the Arabic language, and the meaning is: if you were to ask on supposition, then you would not be answered with "yes," but the answer would be "no." It is thus a challenge to those polytheists who claim to be upon the truth.

﴿Aja'alna﴾ means "We appointed" (sayyarna). (﴿besides the Most Merciful gods to be worshipped﴾. It has been said that it is on its apparent meaning, that the messengers were gathered for him on the night of the Isra' [Night Journey]), because he asked them. But this view is weak, because the hadiths narrated about the Isra' do not contain this. Furthermore, the purpose of the Isra' was to show the honour of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace; indeed, this is one of the purposes of the Isra': to show his superiority over the messengers. So how could this question be directed to them? This view is very weak and has no basis.

It has also been said: the intended meaning is the communities of the two scriptures (Ahl al-Kitab). This is also not correct. These people say the meaning of ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ is: ask the nations to whom they were sent, and these remained until the mission of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. But this is weak and contrary to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. The Qur'an says: ﴿Ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾, and the nations who followed the messengers include polytheists; the Christians, the nearest of the nations, include polytheists. Therefore, their questioning is not directed at them while they are polytheists. This too is weak.

He said: (And he did not ask either of the two opinions, because the purpose of the command to ask is to affirm for the polytheists of Quraysh that no messenger from Allah and no book ever came with worship of other than Allah). This is correct. That is, the question was intended only to bind Quraysh to the fact that no messenger ever came permitting the worship of other than Allah. This is the purpose. It is like His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who recite the Scripture before you﴾ [Yunus 94]. However, the last verse's question is more general, because He said: ﴿ask﴾ those who recite the Scripture before you, and did not restrict it to the messengers.

* In this noble verse there are benefits: it urges the Prophet ﷺ to hold fast to what was revealed to him, and if the Prophet ﷺ is urged to this, then we are more deserving of it.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that Muhammad ﷺ was truly the Messenger of Allah, since the revelation to him is affirmed.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the strengthening of the Prophet ﷺ in holding fast to what was revealed to him, by the fact that he is upon a straight path.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that the Shari'ah brought by Muhammad ﷺ is a straight path with no crookedness or deviation in it.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that this noble Qur'an contains a mention of the Arabs, that is, an honour for them, and a reminder to them; as He said: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ [az-Zukhruf 44].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the placing of a great responsibility upon the Arabs; namely that they will be questioned about this revelation, whether they discharged its rights or did not.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of the greatest proof that none of the earlier messengers said that there are gods worshipped besides Allah; as He said: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers﴾.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the name al-Rahman for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [az-Zukhruf 45]. Al-Rahman is one of the two names that no one else is named by; these are Allah and al-Rahman. Neither of them is used to describe anyone other than Allah. Al-Rahim is used to describe other than Allah, al-'Aziz is used to describe other than Allah, al-Sami' is used to describe other than Allah, and so on; but these two noble names, Allah and al-Rahman, are not attributed to anyone nor named by anyone except Allah alone, with no partner.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the agreement of the messengers upon tawhid. This is like His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya' 25]. This is something upon which the messengers agreed. He also said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut"﴾ [an-Nahl 36]. The messengers came only to reform creation, and creation cannot be reformed or put right except when they establish the tawhid of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If they do not establish His tawhid, their hearts become scattered, and each one goes his own way apart from the other, because every nation wants to have its own particular object of worship, and chaos arises among the servants. But when people unite in worshipping Allah alone, agreement is achieved without chaos.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We certainly sent Musa with Our signs to Fir'awn and his chiefs﴾ [az-Zukhruf 46], and so on to the end.
